title: Convicted Murderer Wins Back Bitcoin Wallet Despite Life Sentence
summary: Convicted killer William Sandeson won a court order for the return of his bitcoin wallet while serving a life sentence for murder. The ruling covered a laptop seized after his arrest, while cash remained withheld. Why the Judge Ordered Sandeson’s Bitcoin Returned William Sandeson secured the return ...
content:
Convicted killer William Sandeson won a court order for the return of his bitcoin wallet while serving a life sentence for murder. The ruling covered a laptop seized after his arrest, while cash remained withheld.

Key Takeaways

  • Sandeson won the return of a bitcoin wallet seized after his 2015 arrest.
  • The judge withheld cash connected to the crime.
  • Prosecutors failed to prove the bitcoin was connected to criminal activity.

Why the Judge Ordered Sandeson’s Bitcoin Returned

William Sandeson secured the return of his bitcoin wallet despite serving a life sentence for murder. Justice John Bodurtha of the Nova Scotia Supreme Court, the Canadian province’s superior trial court, ordered the laptop containing the wallet returned on Nov. 3. Prosecutors had failed to establish that the cryptocurrency was used in the drug transaction, represented criminal proceeds, or was otherwise connected to criminal activity.

Appearing remotely at the Halifax hearing, Sandeson pursued a motion filed in April seeking the return of personal belongings seized following his 2015 arrest. Bodurtha said:

“The potential use of the cryptocurrency as part of the drug transaction is hypothetical … There was no evidence that the respondent actually intended to use it in the transaction.”

Referring to the Crown, the prosecution in Canadian criminal cases, the judge continued his assessment of the evidence. “The Crown cites no evidence of actual dealing with the bitcoin in connection with the murder,” he added.

Bodurtha withheld C$5,000 (approximately US$3,578) in cash found in the apartment, classifying it as offense-related property, meaning property connected to committing a crime. His order directed that the laptop be handed to Sandeson’s family. The laptop’s return concerned bitcoin wallet access, which had also figured in separate civil litigation.

Court Record Details Sandeson’s Convictions

An official court summary of Sandeson’s convictions recorded his first-degree murder conviction in June 2017. An appeals court overturned that verdict in June 2020 and ordered a new trial. The second trial in 2023 resulted in a second-degree murder conviction and a life sentence with parole eligibility set at 15 years. He is serving his sentence in Quebec.

Sandeson and Taylor Samson were Dalhousie University students when the killing occurred in 2015. Sandeson arranged for Samson to visit his apartment to sell him about 18 kilograms of cannabis, then shot him and kept the drugs and money. During his retrial, Sandeson admitted disposing of Samson’s body in the Bay of Fundy; the remains have never been recovered.

Victim’s Family Had Sought to Preserve the Bitcoin

The cryptocurrency had also figured in a wrongful death lawsuit brought by Samson’s mother, Linda Boutilier, and brother, Connor Samson. Their lawyer, James Goodwin, told The Canadian Press in February 2023 that they wanted the bitcoin kept available if they won compensation. The lawsuit sought financial damages for Samson’s death.

Goodwin said a temporary court order obtained in December 2022 had blocked an earlier decision allowing the laptop’s return. In October 2022, Sandeson had told the court his bitcoin was worth C$8,000 to C$10,000. By February 2023, Goodwin suggested the cryptocurrency could exceed C$200,000.

The family’s earlier injunction sought to keep assets available to pay compensation if its lawsuit succeeded, a separate issue from whether prosecutors could retain the bitcoin as crime-related property. A comparable use of an injunction arose in Canadian proceedings targeting cryptocurrency. In 2022, Ottawa residents obtained an Ontario court order freezing assets, including digital currencies, associated with the Freedom Convoy, the trucker-led protests against COVID-19 restrictions.

Preserving a claimant’s ability to collect was also the purpose of a worldwide freezing order against Craig Wright. Britain’s High Court granted that order in July 2024 to secure Peter McCormack’s potential recovery of legal costs amid concerns that assets could be moved. Although the claims differed, that order and the Samson family’s earlier injunction addressed the same practical concern: keeping property available for a possible payment through civil proceedings.

title: Saylor Links Republican and Democratic Wins to Bitcoin Reserves
summary: Michael Saylor cited victories by Republican Byron Donalds in Florida and Democrat James Talarico in Texas as evidence of bipartisan support for government bitcoin holdings. Their legislative records connected the election results to federal and state reserve initiatives. Saylor Cites Republican and...
content:
Michael Saylor cited victories by Republican Byron Donalds in Florida and Democrat James Talarico in Texas as evidence of bipartisan support for government bitcoin holdings. Their legislative records connected the election results to federal and state reserve initiatives.

Key Takeaways

  • Donalds introduced a bill to put the U.S. bitcoin reserve into law.
  • Talarico supported Texas’ bitcoin reserve before winning a Senate seat.
  • The Texas House approved the measure 101-42 in May 2025.

Saylor Cites Republican and Democratic Election Winners

Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), stated Nov. 4 on X that bitcoin reserve support crossed party lines. His assessment followed Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds’ victory in Florida’s gubernatorial election and Democrat James Talarico’s win in the Texas U.S. Senate race.

In his bitcoin reserve statement, Saylor stated:

“Florida elected a Republican governor who backed a U.S. bitcoin reserve. Texas elected a Democratic senator who voted to create one for his state. The case for holding bitcoin crosses party lines.”

Talarico, a Texas state representative, defeated Republican Ken Paxton in the Senate contest. He will replace Republican U.S. Sen. John Cornyn, who lost to Paxton in the primary runoff. The Democrat’s bitcoin reserve vote came during his service in the Texas House, before his election to federal office.

Texas House lawmakers passed Senate Bill 21 on third reading on May 21, 2025. The Texas House voting record lists Talarico among its supporters and records a 101-42 result, with two members present but not voting. The measure subsequently became law, taking effect June 20, 2025.

Texas’ legislation established its Strategic Bitcoin Reserve as a special fund outside the state treasury, administered by the comptroller of public accounts, the state’s chief financial officer. It permits legislative appropriations and imposes eligibility requirements on cryptocurrency purchases. Assets purchased for the reserve must have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the preceding 24 months.

Donalds Pursued Federal Legislation and a Florida Reserve

Donalds introduced legislation to codify the federal bitcoin reserve in March 2025. Codifying the executive initiative would put it into federal law, limiting a future administration’s ability to reverse the policy. His proposal, the Reserve and Stockpile Act, also addressed the government’s holdings of other digital assets.

President Donald Trump had established the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve by executive order on March 6, 2025. The order designated government-owned bitcoin obtained through forfeitures as its initial funding source. It also authorized officials to develop budget-neutral strategies for acquiring more bitcoin without adding costs to taxpayers.

During an Oct. 17 interview, Donalds supported governments assembling bitcoin reserves and referenced proposals for a Florida reserve. He described bitcoin as a potential hedge against monetary policy, meaning protection against risks from central bank decisions, and compared its properties with gold. His argument extended to state governments and included hedging against interest rate exposure.

Bitcoin’s protocol limits on issuance distinguish its supply from currencies issued by central banks. Issuance means the creation of new coins. Current consensus rules, the shared standards participants use to validate transactions and blocks, constrain the total supply to approximately 21 million BTC.

title: India warns AI-powered hackers targeting crypto exchanges at ‘machine speed’
summary: India’s cybersecurity agency says a threat actor is escalating an AI-assisted hacking campaign targeting crypto exchanges and other financial firms.
content:
India’s national cybersecurity agency warned that an AI-assisted threat actor has escalated its attacks on cryptocurrency exchanges and other financial businesses, stealing wallet keys and siphoning funds.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on Wednesday designated the threat actor as “CRAFTY FALCON,” in an update to a campaign it first warned about in October. The latest advisory has now explicitly identified crypto exchanges among affected businesses and detailed the use of AI attack tools. 

“The threat is active and ongoing. CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks, including from NBFCs and fintech entities that had already received the earlier restricted advisories and had undertaken remediation,” said CERT-In. 

The warning adds to evidence of hackers using AI tools against financial institutions. In October, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike reported that an unidentified attacker used ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing tool also named in CERT-In’s advisory, alongside Claude Code and other AI models to breach South Korean financial firms and steal data.

CRAFTY FALCON operates at “machine speed”

CERT-In said the AI-assisted financial threat actor “surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim’s own payment and disbursement APIs.”

The campaign has targeted nonbank lenders, digital lending platforms, fintech companies, payment aggregators and service providers, as well as crypto exchanges. 

According to CERT-In, attackers exploited vulnerable applications and exposed testing environments, using shared credentials and access tokens to move into production systems. They also targeted cloud infrastructure to deploy malicious files. 

AI tools helped attackers rapidly generate and refine attack scripts. The attackers also reverse-engineered application code to develop tailored exploits, while some attacks were timed for weekends and holidays to delay detection. 

Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool

In some incidents, attackers used small test transactions to validate unauthorized transfers before moving larger sums. CERT-In also reported stolen cryptocurrency wallet keys and funds drained from wallets. 

The agency did not name any affected crypto exchanges or quantify losses. 

Cointelegraph reached out to CERT-In, CoinDCX, CoinSwitch, WazirX, ZebPay and Mudrex for comment.

CERT-In has advised entities to “treat this campaign as active and escalating,” urging at-risk companies to heighten security monitoring around the clock, with increased staffing and lowered alert thresholds during holidays, weekends and other low-coverage windows. 

Solana Foundation chief information security officer Michael Coates previously told Cointelegraph that legitimate security teams need access to the strongest AI tools. 

“We need to make sure that the best models we can get are in the hands of defenders because attackers will have something capable enough,” he said.

TRM Labs head of policy Ari Redbord similarly told Cointelegraph in July that “attack techniques are moving faster than a single audit from launch day can account for,” urging continuous security reviews.

title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
American Bitcoin swung to about $126 million in third-quarter net income after a $197.3 million gain on its bitcoin holdings, reversing a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter.
This post American Bitc...
content:
American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue.

The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC.

Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release.

Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market.

A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter

The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives.

Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said.

Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC.

American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain.

Reserve up, satoshis per share up

Management’s preferred yardstick is satoshis per share, which rose about 5% to roughly 11,572 from about 10,989 at the end of June. The share count reflects a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effected earlier this year on July 2.

The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 bitcoin miners with roughly 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end. American Bitcoin remains majority-owned by Hut 8, which on the same day reported its own third-quarter results and confirmed bitcoin sales used to fund share buybacks while shifting mining into the American Bitcoin vehicle.

Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. helped launch the venture with Hut 8 in 2025; earlier Bitcoin Magazine coverage has put the Trump family’s stake near 20%, with Hut 8 holding the rest. The company has climbed the corporate treasury ranks as it stacked coins after its Nasdaq debut.

Whether another quarter of bitcoin price gains can keep paper profits ahead of higher power costs and thinner mining margins is the question the release leaves open.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is above $80,500 and shares of American Bitcoin were down over 5.5% today.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Kiyosaki Buys Bitcoin During Market Panic, Warns of a Bigger Threat
summary: Robert Kiyosaki said he added bitcoin, gold, and silver while others panicked over falling prices. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author tied his purchases to concerns about growing debt and the treatment of workers’ savings under government-issued money. Kiyosaki Reports Buying During Market Declines Robert...
content:
Robert Kiyosaki said he added bitcoin, gold, and silver while others panicked over falling prices. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author tied his purchases to concerns about growing debt and the treatment of workers’ savings under government-issued money.

Key Takeaways

  • Kiyosaki welcomed another crash in bitcoin, gold, and silver.
  • The IMF projected global public debt at 100% of GDP by the decade’s end.
  • His March forecast put bitcoin at $750,000 a year after a global crash.

Kiyosaki Reports Buying During Market Declines

Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad, stated on X on Nov. 4 that he had bought more bitcoin, gold, and silver as other investors panicked. His response to falling asset prices focused on risks he associated with debt and government-issued money. He stated:

“People panicked when gold, silver, bitcoin crash. I bought more.”

Growing global debt, especially in the United States, was the central problem in his assessment. The author criticized political leaders for failing to take the steps he considered necessary to address it. He also characterized fiat currency as a means of taking wealth from people who worked for money and saved their earnings.

Education featured in that criticism through his contention that education taught nothing about money. His emphasis on financial education accompanied his objections to leadership and the monetary system. Together, those concerns formed his explanation for continuing to buy assets despite the declines that had frightened other investors.

Global Debt Adds Context to His Monetary Concerns

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) separately highlighted rising fiscal risks in briefing remarks released Oct. 16. Its global public debt projection put the ratio at 100% of gross domestic product by the end of the decade. The fund called for countries with elevated debt or high risk to begin fiscal consolidation, supported by credible plans and realistic assumptions.

An Oct. 3 statement illustrated how Kiyosaki viewed holding bitcoin and precious metals as financial preparation. Responding to a woman who questioned whether anticipating trouble was pessimistic, he compared financial precautions with carrying car insurance. He asked about her ownership of those assets and expressed a preference for money governments could not print.

That insurance comparison addressed protection against economic disruption, while his February comments focused on entry prices. On Feb. 1, he drew a comparison between market crashes and retail sales, contrasting shoppers who welcomed discounts with investors who sold falling assets. At that point, he described holding cash while waiting to buy more gold, silver, and bitcoin.

Earlier Purchases and Post-Crash Price Targets

A subsequent statement supplied a specific example of that buying approach. On Feb. 20, Kiyosaki disclosed buying one bitcoin for $67,000 as its price fell. He linked the purchase to expectations that U.S. debt would weaken the dollar and prompt the Federal Reserve to create more money.

By March 16, his post-crash cryptocurrency forecast put bitcoin at $750,000 and ethereum at $95,000 one year after a global financial crash. The same scenario included gold at $35,000 per ounce and silver at $200. Returning to the prospect of another decline on Nov. 4, he stated:

“Can’t wait for the next crash of gold, silver, bitcoin.”

title: Analyst Sees Bitcoin Rally Potential Despite Democratic Sweep
summary: Bitcoin could see a relief rally as U.S. midterm election uncertainty clears, with a Democratic sweep largely priced in, an analyst said. He warned that slower crypto reform could weigh more heavily on companies awaiting regulatory permissions. Analyst Sees Room for a Bitcoin Relief Rally James Butt...
content:
Bitcoin could see a relief rally as U.S. midterm election uncertainty clears, with a Democratic sweep largely priced in, an analyst said. He warned that slower crypto reform could weigh more heavily on companies awaiting regulatory permissions.

Key Takeaways

  • Democratic control of Congress could complicate CLARITY Act passage.
  • U.S. crypto equities could be more sensitive to the result than bitcoin.
  • Compliant operators could gain from greater scrutiny of competitors.

Analyst Sees Room for a Bitcoin Relief Rally

James Butterfill, head of research at digital asset investment firm Coinshares, assessed the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm election results in comments sent directly to Bitcoin.com News. He stated:

“My sense is that bitcoin had largely priced in a Democratic sweep, leaving room for a relief rally as uncertainty clears. Therefore, the anticipated result need not trigger another sell-off.”

Democrats won majorities in both the House and Senate. The incoming majorities take office in January, setting up divided government for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term. His administration will face an opposition-controlled Congress as it pursues its legislative agenda.

Bitcoin was trading near $80,574 at 7:12 p.m. EST on Nov. 4, up 4.20% over 24 hours. The price had rebounded from a 24-hour low of $75,618 and was approaching a 24-hour high of $81,105.

Crypto Stocks Could Face Greater Regulatory Exposure

Turning to legislation, Butterfill warned:

“The greater concern is slower crypto reform. CLARITY faces a harder path, while investigations into Trump-linked ventures could consume political capital and generate uncomfortable headlines across the sector.”

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, known as CLARITY, would define how federal securities and commodities regulators oversee crypto assets and trading platforms. U.S. Rep. French Hill had sought CLARITY Act approval after the midterms following the bill’s failure to clear a Senate procedural hurdle in September.

Existing policy offered some continuity: “But the administration remains in place, and existing regulatory progress, including GENIUS, does not simply disappear.” Trump signed the GENIUS Act into law on July 18, 2025, establishing a regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, tokens designed to track currencies such as the U.S. dollar.

U.S. crypto equities would be more sensitive than bitcoin, he expected, particularly exchanges, token issuers, and businesses reliant on new regulatory permissions. Established, compliant operators could gain if scrutiny disproportionately affected weaker competitors, he suggested.

Miners faced a different source of demand in his assessment. He anticipated that those with existing data centers would remain in demand from AI hyperscalers, large technology companies operating extensive cloud and artificial intelligence computing infrastructure.

Liquidity and Fund Flows Remain Central to Bitcoin Outlook

Monetary conditions remained central to his bitcoin outlook. The Coinshares head of research noted:

“For bitcoin, real yields, dollar liquidity and ETP flows still carry more weight than the elections.”

Real yields measure bond returns after adjusting for inflation. Exchange-traded products (ETPs) include bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which provide investment exposure through brokerage accounts.

Investor withdrawals continued into election day. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $115.56 million in net outflows on Nov. 3, extending withdrawals to three sessions. The daily outflow was down from $398.62 million on Nov. 2.

A similar emphasis on liquidity appeared in Arthur Hayes’ assessment of bank balance sheets. Hayes tied renewed bitcoin strength to balance sheet expansion by commercial banks or the Federal Reserve.

Falling oil prices could ease inflation pressure and moderate expectations for interest rate increases, Butterfill said. His longer-term assessment remained favorable toward institutional adoption: “I would temper expectations for the pace of US reform, while remaining constructive on institutional adoption. How Trump responds to being constrained is the less predictable part.”

title: Crypto Industry Braces for Tougher Rules After Democrats Dominate Midterms
summary: Democrats’ midterm election victories, which secured the party control of both the Senate and House of Representatives, are expected to reshape legislative priorities, with greater emphasis on stricter oversight of emerging technologies.   Democratic Midterm Victories Reshape Tech Policy Democrats’ ...
content:
Democrats’ midterm election victories, which secured the party control of both the Senate and House of Representatives, are expected to reshape legislative priorities, with greater emphasis on stricter oversight of emerging technologies.

Key Takeaways

  • Following 2026 midterms, Democrats secured Congress, raising the prospects for digital assets.
  • The CLARITY Act faces expiration on Jan. 3, 2027 without 60-vote bipartisan support.
  • Sen. Elizabeth Warren is expected to lead the Senate Banking Committee, signaling strict SEC enforcement and AI safeguards in 2027.

Democratic Midterm Victories Reshape Tech Policy

Democrats’ victories in the U.S. midterm elections, which secured the party control of both the Senate and House of Representatives, have reshaped the political landscape surrounding emerging technologies and digital assets. According to industry advocacy group The Digital Chamber (TDC), the shift in congressional leadership leaves key regulatory legislation, most notably the CLARITY Act, at a critical juncture.

After failing to clear the Senate’s 60-vote procedural threshold in a 49-50 vote, the current version of the CLARITY Act—the proposed crypto market structure bill—faces expiration when the 119th Congress concludes on Jan. 3, 2027. Advancing the legislation in the next Congress would require lawmakers to reintroduce the bill and negotiate a new agreement.

However, because Senate rules generally require 60 votes to overcome a filibuster, the incoming Democratic majority will need broad bipartisan support to advance crypto market structure legislation. Market analysts expect any revived version of the bill under Democratic control to include tighter compliance standards, stronger consumer protections, and stricter decentralized finance (DeFi) regulations.

The election results have implications beyond a single bill, potentially reshaping the broader regulatory environment for blockchain technology and artificial intelligence (AI). With Democrats taking control of both chambers, leadership changes on key congressional committees are expected to shift legislative priorities toward greater oversight.

With crypto critic Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) expected to take the helm of the Senate Banking Committee, TDC anticipates a swift pivot from deregulation toward tighter oversight of digital asset exchanges and their integration into the broader banking system. TDC also predicts the House Financial Services Committee will shift its priorities toward enforcing strict stablecoin reserve requirements, expanding consumer disclosures and strengthening anti-money laundering (AML) controls over rapid market expansion.

Navigating Regulatory Uncertainty and U.S. Competitiveness

Although cryptocurrency industry advocacy groups spent heavily during the 2026 election cycle to support pro-innovation candidates, the electoral setbacks mean federal regulators will have to rely primarily on enforcement actions in the absence of comprehensive legislation.

Meanwhile, as AI infrastructure expands, the incoming Congress is expected to place greater emphasis on safeguards addressing data privacy and national security risks associated with advanced AI deployment. Democratic lawmakers are also expected to push for formal risk management frameworks and greater transparency across high-stakes AI applications.

While the political realignment creates near-term regulatory uncertainty, technology policy advocates acknowledge that lawmakers on both sides of the aisle recognize the need for clear, transparent rules. Whether Congress revives the CLARITY Act during the lame-duck session or develops new legislation in 2027, the future of U.S. technological innovation could hinge on Washington’s ability to balance consumer protection with global competitiveness.

title: Mercado Bitcoin says phased reopening to begin Monday, will cover losses
summary: Customers will initially be able to view their holdings, while withdrawals and trading remain suspended pending security checks.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 4, 2026

Customers will initially be able to view their holdings, while withdrawals and trading remain suspended pending security checks.

Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin said it will begin restoring customer account access Monday after a hack that blockchain analysts estimated resulted in more than $46 million in stolen assets.

In a statement to Cointelegraph, Mercado Bitcoin said customers would initially regain access through its website to view balances, statements, holdings and investments. Transfers, withdrawals and trading will resume in later phases, subject to independent security testing.

Mercado Bitcoin also pledged to use company funds to replenish assets affected by the breach, saying more than $15 million in stolen funds had already been frozen with help from the industry.

“Our trading desk is preparing to begin the necessary repurchases in domestic and international markets,” it said.

The update follows the exchange’s disclosure of a security breach on Monday, which saw attackers transferring funds from the company’s hot wallets and customer deposit addresses through standard transfers.

Addressing liquidity, Mercado said it had a strong cash position, bolstered by a $20 million investment from stablecoin issuer Tether to support operational expansion.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Bitcoin climbed above $80,500 as US stocks rallied following the midterm elections. Democrats won control of Congress, raising doubts about the future of the CLARITY bill, while ZachXBT identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million.

Bitcoin hits $80.5K as US stocks rally on midterm election results

Bitcoin (BTC) returned to $80,000 at Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks surged following a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections.

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD up by over 4%, having rebounded from its lowest levels in seven weeks.

Data from CoinGlass showed the price dip liquidating late BTC long positions below $76,000, while a wall of asks kept upside contained below $78,000. Total crypto long liquidations over the past 24 hours stood at $288 million.

US stock futures made swift gains on Wednesday after initially dipping overnight. S&P 500 futures fell as low as 7,490 points, their lowest level since July 31, before reaching 7,690 points, approaching new month-to-date highs.

In comments sent to Cointelegraph, James Butterfill, head of research at crypto asset manager CoinShares, saw the potential for a wider Bitcoin “relief rally” as election uncertainty faded.

Democrats win Congress as CLARITY bill faces fresh doubts

Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections, giving the party greater influence over crypto legislation and oversight of President Donald Trump’s administration.

At the time of writing, Democrats had secured 228 House seats to Republicans’ 139, with 68 races still uncalled, according to the Associated Press. The Senate tally stood at 54 seats for Democrats and 44 for Republicans.

The result could derail the CLARITY crypto market structure bill, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK.

“The immediate read on this election result is that CLARITY bill is likely dead,” he said in comments shared with Cointelegraph, referring to both the upcoming lame-duck session and the next Congress.

Muehlbauer said he expected Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Maxine Waters, both outspoken crypto critics, to chair the Senate Banking Committee and House Financial Services Committee, respectively. Democratic control could also bring greater congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked digital asset businesses.

ZachXBT identifies French bank as alleged victim of $133M crypto theft

Onchain investigator ZachXBT has identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million, warning that total losses could be higher. 

On Wednesday, the pseudonymous crypto sleuth said the institution, which he described as having $235 billion in assets, was allegedly exploited over multiple days. He also suggested that additional losses may have occurred through over-the-counter (OTC) transactions that were not included in earlier estimates. 

“I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity,” ZachXBT said.

The bank’s alleged involvement has not been independently verified, and ZachXBT has not disclosed how the attackers gained access to the funds. 

The disclosure follows ZachXBT’s initial report on Monday, when he identified over $106 million in suspicious withdrawals from centralized exchanges. 

On Tuesday, he raised the estimated losses to over $133 million after discovering another $27 million in withdrawals, some of which occurred after his initial warning.

title: BitMart founder says security team ‘severely understaffed’ after new hack
summary: The crypto exchange’s founder warned of security staffing shortages amid restructuring as analysts flagged suspicious transfers potentially linked to the Mercado Bitcoin hack.
content:
Cryptocurrency exchange BitMart is operating with an understaffed security team following restructuring, its founder said Wednesday, after confirming a new hack that may be linked to the recent attack on Brazil’s exchange Mercado Bitcoin.

In a post on X, BitMart founder Sheldon Xia said threats against employees and alleged retaliation by former staff had complicated efforts to retain technical personnel.

“It took considerable effort and individual conversations to persuade some key technical staff to remain and maintain our core systems,” Xia wrote. “However, we continue to face numerous attacks. Our security team is currently severely understaffed, but we are still doing everything we can to safeguard data and assets.”

Xia described the amount involved in Monday’s hack as small but did not disclose a figure. Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery identified approximately $391,000 in suspicious transfers from wallets mostly associated with BitMart across three blockchains, according to a Wednesday investigation.

Source: Sheldon Xia

Bitquery traced the funds to a wallet also implicated in the more than $46 million Mercado Bitcoin hack on Monday, Nov. 2, supporting Xia’s preliminary suspicion of a possible connection between the incidents.

Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US

BitMart weighs restructuring after shutdown announcement

The latest breach comes amid months of uncertainty over BitMart’s future. The exchange announced in July that it would end trading on Aug. 26 and cease operations in January 2027. Following the announcement, users reported delayed withdrawals and frozen accounts, raising concerns about access to their funds.

In August, BitMart’s Chinese-language X account alleged that employees had gone unpaid and demanded answers about customer funds. The founder dismissed the allegations as fabricated, though it remained unclear who controlled the account at the time.

In a restructuring proposal published Monday, the exchange outlined three potential recovery options for users, including liquid asset distributions and recovery-linked tokens, with plans to seek court approval in December or January.

Cointelegraph contacted BitMart for details about the restructuring, security staffing and latest breach but had not received a response by publication.

Crypto crime-fighting alliance disbands amid wave of hacks

Separately, a crypto crime-fighting alliance formed by Tron, Tether and TRM Labs has dissolved amid a wave of major industry hacks, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.

The T3 Financial Crime Unit, launched in September 2024 and later joined by Binance, struggled with slow responses and poor coordination, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. One source said the group disbanded in late August.

In May, T3 said it had helped freeze more than $450 million in assets linked to suspected criminal activity since its launch in 2024.

The group’s dissolution comes amid a wave of major crypto hacks, including last week’s $6.3 billion Binance breach, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

title: Morgan Stanley Among First to Adopt DTCC’s Tokenization Service
summary: Morgan Stanley said it is among the first major financial institutions to tokenize real-world assets using the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation’s newly launched Tokenization Service. Digitizing Legacy Instruments Wall Street giant Morgan Stanley announced Nov. 4 that it is among the first m...
content:
Morgan Stanley said it is among the first major financial institutions to tokenize real-world assets using the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation’s newly launched Tokenization Service.

Key Takeaways

  • Morgan Stanley said it the among first banks to tokenize U.S. equities and Treasuries via DTCC’s new DTS platform.
  • Launched on Oct. 28, DTCC’s DTS platform targets three core goals to boost institutional market liquidity.
  • Analysts view Morgan Stanley’s 2024 deployment as a crucial first test for scaling tokenized assets.

Digitizing Legacy Instruments

Wall Street giant Morgan Stanley announced Nov. 4 that it is among the first major financial institutions to tokenize real-world assets (RWAs) following the official debut of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation Tokenization Service (DTS). The move marks a major leap forward in bringing mainstream financial instruments onto digital rails.

According to the firm, Morgan Stanley has begun utilizing the platform to create tokenized representations of U.S. equities and U.S. Treasury securities. By mapping traditional, highly regulated financial assets onto distributed ledger networks, the initiative bridges legacy settlement systems with modern programmable infrastructure.

The integration follows the official commercial launch of the DTCS on Oct. 28. Built to process securities held in custody by the Depository Trust Company (DTC), the tokenization platform enables institutions to issue and manage digital representations of assets securely.

When the DTCC rolled out DTS, which initially connects to the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu blockchain, the clearing and settlement platform outlined a clear vision centered on modernizing market infrastructure. According to the DTCC’s statements, the platform was designed to address structural bottlenecks in legacy trading environments by achieving three core objectives, namely enhancing asset liquidity and boosting collateral mobility.

The platform also aims to reduce operational overhead and settlement friction, allowing institutions to optimize how capital is deployed across trading operations.

Shift to Production-Grade Workflows

Morgan Stanley’s adoption highlights a broader macro trend across global banking: a steady migration from exploratory proofs-of-concept to live, production-grade operational workflows. Amy Oldenburg, head of digital assets strategy at Morgan Stanley, noted that the integration will influence how the firm builds out its digital asset capabilities as market structures evolve.

“The hands-on experience of integrating tokenized securities with established market infrastructure will inform the continued development of the firm’s digital asset capabilities as the market evolves,” Oldenburg said in a statement.

As major financial institutions like Morgan Stanley, alongside other early adopters, begin testing and deploying tokenized equities and Treasuries at scale, industry watchers view the DTCC’s DTS as a critical proving ground for whether blockchain technology can successfully scale within the plumbing of global traditional finance.

title: Crypto PACs eye 2028 ‘new map’ as Democrats take Congress
summary: Crypto super PACs spent more than $176 million on the midterms, but the Democratic sweep raises the prospect of tougher industry scrutiny.
content:
Two years after crypto money helped drive Sherrod Brown out of the Senate, roughly $64 million couldn’t keep him from returning.

Brown’s victory over Republican Jon Husted in Ohio delivered the industry its biggest electoral loss of the 2026 midterms as Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The sweep also puts Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s fiercest critics, in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee.

Crypto super PACs spent about $176 million across 100 seats during the election cycle, including primaries, according to Reuters, up from more than $130 million in 2024. Fairshake and its affiliated PACs accounted for $154.5 million across 89 races.

“The next Congress will bring a fundamentally different environment for crypto in Washington, and the industry should expect significantly more scrutiny,” Kyle Bligen, executive director at the Decentralization Research Center, told Cointelegraph.

Fairshake, meanwhile, is left with more than $67 million heading to the 2028 elections. “Newly elected and current members will have a choice: protect consumers and American jobs or fight progress,” spokesperson Geoff Vetter told Cointelegraph in an email. “We will be watching and ‘28 is a new map.”

Crypto’s $64 million bet in Ohio

Ohio was the industry’s biggest bet as crypto PACs put more than $64 million into keeping Senator Jon Husted in office. His opponent, former Sen. Sherrod Brown, won the special election to complete former Sen. JD Vance’s term, which ends in January 2029. He could seek a senior role on the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

Brown’s comeback came two years after crypto’s biggest win in 2024, when Fairshake spent $40 million to help Bernie Moreno unseat him in Ohio’s other Senate seat. Some industry leaders treated that result as a warning to Congress. Gemini exchange co-founder Cameron Winklevoss declared on X: “This is what happens when you mess with the crypto army”.

This year, crypto spending was part of a much larger flood of outside money. Independent expenditures in the race topped $350 million, while Brown turned the crypto spending into a campaign theme, writing “I’ll be damned if crypto billionaires decide this race,” in a campaign message.

The loss in Ohio may weaken the perception that defying crypto PACs carries an electoral cost in Washington. Before the vote, a Republican crypto lobbyist told Politico that a Brown win would “neuter Fairshake’s perceived Sword of Damocles.”

Where the money went

Nebraska, meanwhile, offered crypto PACs a significant win, with Sen. Pete Ricketts retaining his seat after Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs spent $13.5 million opposing independent challenger Dan Osborn.

“As the biggest spender in the Nebraska Senate race, we’re proud to have helped Sen. Ricketts weather the waves of a hard-fought cycle,” wrote Vetter. “Fairshake played a meaningful role in winning competitive races across the country in 2026 and we will do it again in 2028.” The PAC’s other Senate wins came in Republican strongholds, including Barry Moore in Alabama and Andy Barr in Kentucky.

Other spending failed to deliver the intended results, both in primaries and in November. The Fairshake network’s roughly $10 million spent opposing Juliana Stratton in the Illinois Democratic primary failed to block her nomination. She later won the Senate seat. In Massachusetts, John Deaton lost despite roughly $700,000 in spending by crypto-backed Commonwealth Unity Fund to help elect him. Ken Paxton, who received crypto PAC backing in his successful Texas Republican runoff against John Cornyn, went on to lose to James Talarico.

The House brought another setback when digital assets subcommittee chair Bryan Steil lost to Democrat Mitchell Berman despite $1.9 million in crypto PAC funding.

The road ahead for crypto

The shift in congressional control could slow crypto legislation, but BitGo CEO and co-founder Mike Belshe said the election results would not alter the industry’s trajectory. “Crypto has continued to move forward under different administrations and different political majorities. The GENIUS Act is now law, stablecoin rules are moving ahead, and regulators are continuing to work on tokenization and digital asset markets.”

Democratic victories could also bring crypto supporters into the Senate. Advocacy group Stand With Crypto counted 19 winning Senate candidates it classified as pro-crypto and eight as anti-crypto, with 33 of the 35 Senate races called as of 9:45 p.m. UTC on Nov. 4.

Despite the crypto PAC spending against him in Texas, Talarico voted for the Texas Bitcoin reserve as a state lawmaker and is rated by the group as strongly supportive of crypto.

For industry advocates, the next challenge is building relationships with incoming lawmakers. Jessica Martinez, US policy director at Fireblocks, told Cointelegraph that many newly elected members had limited records on crypto, making “educating members early” key to shaping the Democratic policy agenda.

title: Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority
A federal judge refused to halt stock perpetual futures on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial but found a Cboe- and Citadel Securities-backed group likely to prove the CFTC exceed...
content:
Stock perpetual futures can keep trading on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial for now after a federal judge denied an emergency bid to halt them Tuesday, while finding that the Wall Street-backed challengers are likely to prove the CFTC overstepped its authority.

U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges.

The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford.

The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges.

Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms.

“Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote.

Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.”

The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.”

What the ruling does and does not do

The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction.

The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case.

Kalshi was already listing four single-stock perps on Qualcomm, McDonald’s, Amgen and Costco by Wednesday morning, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times.

Bloomberg Law reported that the judge signaled she might ultimately side with the Wall Street firms opposed to the products.

A CFTC-SEC turf fight with crypto venues in the middle

The fight is over a label. Selig’s Nov. 3 statement said the contracts were deemed approved under Commission Regulation 40.3 as security futures products, a category the CFTC and SEC oversee jointly. The exchanges filed them Sept. 18, and the agency let its 45-day review period lapse without a written order.

The alliance argues that a contract with no expiration date and no delivery obligation is a security-based swap. Congress limited retail trading in those to national securities exchanges under full SEC oversight.

Its complaint says the CFTC “invited a parallel, synthetic market in U.S. stocks to grow outside the exclusive jurisdiction” of the SEC.

A CFTC spokesperson called the lawsuit “troubling” and told Reuters: “Our markets should be governed by law, not litigation campaigns intended to block innovation.”

For crypto-native venues, the stakes reach past stocks. Perpetuals are the core product of crypto derivatives trading, and Kalshi and Coinbase have used the CFTC’s framework to bring them onshore.

The agency approved the first U.S.-listed bitcoin perpetual on May 29, and Kalshi went live with the product soon after.

That approval already faces a challenge. CME Group sued the CFTC in June, arguing that a contract built on exchanged funding payments is a swap, not a future. That case is pending in Washington.

The New York order covers security futures, not commodities like bitcoin. But a federal judge has now said, at least preliminarily, that a contract with no expiration does not look like a future.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: How Aussie Bitcoiners can avoid 2027’s shock CGT hike
summary: From setting up an SMSF or a company, to just leaving the country entirely, here are some strategies Australian Bitcoiners can employ to deal with 2027’s massive CGT hike.
content:
The Australian government’s decision to scrap the 50% capital gains discount for all investments in the May budget came as a big shock for crypto owners. The new scheme effectively doubles the taxable component of a gain, minus a small discount for inflation.

But there are legal ways to minimize the amount of CGT you’ll have to pay — if you start prepping now.

Some Aussie crypto holders are taking drastic measures — like Finder founder and crypto king Fred Schebesta who is relocating to Singapore which offers 0% CGT, stating the tax changes were a “killer blow.”

But there are less dramatic methods to reduce your CGT bills including setting up a self managed super fund (SMSF), a company to trade crypto at the company tax rate, or to just cross your fingers and hope the opposition will reverse the changes after the next election.

Source: YahooFinance

What’s changing with CGT on July 1, 2027?

Since 1999, Aussie asset owners have only paid tax on half of their capital gain. From July 1, 2027 they’ll pay their full income tax rate — which means 30% CGT if your income and gains are between A$45,000 and $135,000, 37% for the portion between $135,000 and $190,000 and 47% above that. (All figures in this story are in Aussie dollars)

Adding insult to injury, low-income earners who aren’t on welfare like students and retirees will pay a minimum 30% CGT rate no matter how little the gain.

The only discount now available accounts for the effect of inflation on your cost basis. So if you buy a house for $1 million in 2027 and sell it for $1.5 million after 10 years, with inflation at 3%, you won’t have to pay tax on the $344,000 or so attributed to inflation.

“The challenge for cryptocurrency is that the CGT changes, indexation really helps slower growing assets not fast ones,” explains Andrea Yuen, Swyftx CEO.

So if you bought Bitcoin for $10,000 and sell it ten years later for $100,000, the inflation discount is only around $3,439. Under the old system you would pay tax on $45,000 of gains. Under the new system you’ll pay tax on $86,561 of gains.

Stockspot analyst Chris Bryki compared how ten different asset classes would fare under the new rules.

“Crypto sits at the bottom because almost its entire return comes from capital growth,” he wrote in The Australian newspaper.

“An already speculative investment is about to become less rewarding after tax.”

Here are a few different strategies to help crypto holders deal with the changes, ranging from little to no effort, to restructuring your entire life.

1. Hope for a massive bull run before July

Any gain you’ve made before July 1 2027 will be taxed under the existing 50% discount scheme. So your best bet is to hope a raging bull market pushes the value of your portfolio as high as possible before that date.

You should faithfully record the value of every crypto asset you have that day, as any gain from that value will be taxed at the higher rate.

Ben Simpson, founder of crypto advisory service Collective Shift, says Bitcoin’s performance since mid-year in a challenging macro environment bodes well for further gains before July.

But Simpson (who points out he’s not a financial advisor) adds, “I probably wouldn’t be betting the farm on the fact that we’re gonna have a huge bull run”

“I think the halving in May 2028 is where we’ll see most of the returns. So I don’t think it’s going to work in investors’ favor.”

Yuen notes that prices aren’t within your control.  “A strategy isn’t a strategy if you’re just sort of hoping,” she says.

2. Vote for a party that will reverse the CGT changes

Both the official opposition The Coalition, and the insurgent opposition One Nation, have promised to reverse the changes. Crypto voters who feel strongly enough about this single issue, could vote for a change in government.

However, the ruling ALP holds 94 out of 150 seats in the House of Representatives and will be difficult to dislodge from office. If the government does change — and the legislation can pass the Senate in time — it’s technically possible the changes could be reversed before anyone has to file taxes from July 1 2028.

But it’s probably more likely that any change to the system would occur after that date. Adrian Forza, director of Crypto Tax Australia, says this would make calculating gains very difficult.

“It would be a nightmare to do three calculations, but longer term, it’ll be better for the public.”

3. Shift your crypto into a self-managed superannuation fund

Australian retirement funds are called superannuation funds, and once you are over 60 you can access your investments tax-free — even as they keep growing.

Unfortunately none of the retail super funds allow clients to invest in crypto, so if you want to protect your crypto gains using this method, you’d have to set up an SMSF. About a third of Simpson’s high net worth clients invest in crypto via SMSFs. 

“Buying Bitcoin and accumulating it there is a super solid idea,” he says, although he cautions against adding many altcoins. “You’re risking your retirement, which is an ultra long-term hold, on short-term altcoins,” he says.

Australian super fund AMP has invested in Bitcoin — but doesn’t allow its clients to do so.

The big drawback with SMSFs — explains the 27-year-old founder — is that younger crypto investors can’t access the money for decades.

“You can’t touch it until you’re in retirement, right? So you can’t really utilize any of those gains until later in life.”

Realistically then, it’s a strategy more suited to wealthier investors aged over 50, who have a shorter period to wait. 

Related: Older investors are risking everything for a crypto-funded retirement

The government has also made running an SMSF a pain in the backside, with lots of compliance paperwork and audits, as well as a bunch of unavoidable fees that make it prohibitive for smaller balances.
Annual costs typically range between $2,000 and $4,000, although online providers like Stake can reduce total annual costs to around $1,330, as long as you only buy Bitcoin or Ether ETFs.

You also have to sell any crypto and pay tax on it before you can rebuy it with your SMSF, and there are annual contribution limits to factor in, although Forza says you should be able to get almost $400,000 in there with a bit of creativity. 

Keep an eye out in December for a detailed report on how to set up a crypto SMSF.

4. Borrow against your Bitcoin to avoid a CGT event

A strategy some billionaires employ to avoid paying tax is by borrowing against their assets, as repaying the loan often works out cheaper than paying tax on a sale.

Bitcoiners can now access a range of lenders, including BlockEarner, Vield and Swyftx, that let you employ a similar strategy by borrowing against your BTC as collateral. 

“We like to bring that strategy to the masses, not just to billionaires,” laughs Yuen.

But it can be risky if you don’t have a billionaire’s deep pockets. Borrowers face high interest rates, relatively short loan periods (typically 12 months), and risk losing their Bitcoin if the market moves against them. You can’t borrow against the full value either — Swyftx has a loan-to-value ratio around 40%.

”If your collateral drops below a certain amount, there will be a margin call,” she says.  “I would say it’s a bet on a price going up. I think you have to have a view that crypto will go up — or at least not go down so that you get margin-called... Otherwise, a crypto-backed loan wouldn’t make sense for you.”

Simpson doesn’t recommend this strategy due to the risks, but says it can pay off for some people. For example if you borrow at 10% interest, and Bitcoin compounds by 33% a year (as it has done in the past) you’d end up much better off than paying CGT. 

But he warns it’s a leveraged bet that is best suited to sophisticated investors.

“I wouldn’t recommend it for someone that’s highly exposed to crypto and doesn’t have the capital behind them because it’s a risky thing if you don’t know what you’re doing.”

Bitcoin is down 28% over the past year, so anyone borrowing a year ago would have faced margin calls and possible liquidation as well as interest costs.

Borrowing against Bitcoin for a house deposit has become a more popular strategy. (BlockEarner)

Forza cautions that borrowing crypto can also be a CGT event in some circumstances, such as borrowing in DeFi. If you deposit ETH to Aave, it gets automatically swapped to WETH which  is a taxable event, and when you withdraw the ETH it’s another taxable event. 

Borrowing from centralized lenders like BlockEarner or Swyftx is currently a grey area, and the ATO has not clarified if it’s a taxable event.

”If you’re talking about [borrowing] ten grand fine. But if you’ve got three to five Bitcoin, I wouldn’t risk it because if it goes against you then you’re going to be paying tax.”

”Vield is the only one in Australia that’s got a private ruling that says their product is not a taxable event. No one else has got one.”

Swftxy confirmed it has not got a private ruling and said clients should seek tax advice, while BlockEarner did not respond to a request for comment. 

In part two of our Aussie CGT special, coming later this week, we’ll bring you the final four strategies to minimize your crypto tax bills, including setting up a company or leaving the country entirely.

Also read: Baby boomers worth $79T are finally getting on board with Bitcoin

title: Bitcoin Fork ECX Price Crashes 76% From Peak as Binance Hack Steals Spotlight
summary: The recent $6.3 billion Binance hack and subsequent cryptocurrency market downturn largely eclipsed Drivechain creator Paul Sztorc’s ECX launch on Oct. 29, 2026. Since the start of the phased launch and subsequent trading, the forked digital asset climbed to an all-time high of $134.97 per coin befo...
content:
The recent $6.3 billion Binance hack and subsequent cryptocurrency market downturn largely eclipsed Drivechain creator Paul Sztorc’s ECX launch on Oct. 29, 2026. Since the start of the phased launch and subsequent trading, the forked digital asset climbed to an all-time high of $134.97 per coin before relinquishing 76% of its peak valuation, leaving it exchanging hands near $32 at press time.

Key Takeaways

  • The $6.3 billion Binance hack overshadowed ECX’s debut, leaving its ambitious launch largely unnoticed.
  • ECX commands a $639 million valuation, but its thin liquidity tells a more complicated story.
  • Bitcoin forks face an uncomfortable reality in 2026, where market value matters more than technical pedigree.

Paul Sztorc’s Ecash Fork Debuts Amid Market Turmoil

At 4:15 p.m. Eastern time on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, ecash (ECX) was trading just above $32, having surrendered nearly 31% of its value over the preceding 24 hours. ECX serves as the native token of the Ecash blockchain, a Bitcoin fork spearheaded by Layertwo Labs founder Paul Sztorc.

Unlike the recent BIP110-Bitcoin Knots fork associated with Luke Dashjr, Sztorc’s ECX fork was deliberately orchestrated, granting nearly every BTC holder—with the exception of Satoshi Nakamoto—an equivalent ECX balance at a 1:1 ratio.

The blockchain’s rollout unfolded across three distinct phases, culminating in its mainnet debut on Oct. 29, 2026, coinciding with the 18th anniversary of the Bitcoin white paper the following day. By Nov. 4, 2026, the Ecash mainnet was actively producing blocks, supported by approximately 943 petahash per second (PH/s) of computing power, approaching the 1 exahash per second (EH/s) threshold.

Trading near $32 per ECX on Wednesday, the digital asset commands a market capitalization of approximately $639 million. That would put it near the bottom of the top 100 overall cryptocurrencies by market cap. Exchange support for ECX remains super limited, although Neoxa Exchange facilitates ecash trading, much like its support for the BIP110 fork. ECX’s USDC trading pair ranks as Neoxa’s third most active market by trading volume.

Did Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Bury ECX’s Debut?

ECX’s official rollout proved decidedly lackluster, as the Binance hack eclipsed the Ecash mainnet debut on the very same day, commanding vastly greater attention across the cryptocurrency industry. Even Luke Dashjr and the BIP110 faction’s fork appeared to attract considerably more publicity than Sztorc’s deliberately planned Bitcoin fork.

It’s safe to say that market participants were largely preoccupied with the $6.3 billion breach of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and its potential ramifications for the broader industry and digital asset markets.

Bitcoin Forks Face an Unforgiving Market in 2026

Among Bitcoin and its forks only, the newly launched token still ranks fourth by market capitalization (per eCash’s own website), behind bitcoin, bitcoin blake2b, and bitcoin cash. Bitcoin SV and the earlier Ecash blockchain, which split from bitcoin cash, both command market valuations below ECX. Nevertheless, almost all of those established networks have achieved considerably broader adoption than the newly introduced Ecash ledger, while Bitcoin Blake2b, trading under the tickers BTCB2 or the controversial XBT, also commands a higher price per coin.

While ECX changes hands near $32, BTCB2 commands a substantially higher price of $317 per coin at press time. Both assets inhabit sparsely adopted ecosystems, with limited exchange support and liquidity thinner than a strand of hair. Under such precarious trading conditions, even modest exchange swaps can send valuations careening faster than the Road Runner outsmarting Wile E. Coyote.

The broader lesson is that clever token distribution and marketing alone cannot conjure market relevance. A blockchain fork introduced amid an industry crisis must ultimately prove its worth through liquidity, exchange listings, and authentic demand rather than its technical lineage. Unless ECX cultivates meaningful utility and secures wider exchange access, even its initial valuation may prove little more than speculative noise.

title: Huizenga Loses House Seat Despite $1 Million From Crypto PAC Fairshake
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Huizenga Loses House Seat Despite $1 Million From Crypto PAC Fairshake
Rep. Bill Huizenga, vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee, lost despite $1 million from Fairshake.
This post Huizenga Loses House Seat Despite $1 Million From Crypto PAC Fairshake first appeared o...
content:
Rep. Bill Huizenga, the No. 2 Republican on the House Financial Services Committee, lost his reelection bid to Democrat Sean McCann, the Associated Press called Wednesday afternoon, despite about $1 million in support from the crypto super PAC Fairshake.

With more than 97% of votes counted earlier today, McCann led Huizenga 50.1% to 48.3% in Michigan’s 4th Congressional District, a gap of about 7,000 votes out of nearly 300,000 cast. The race had been rated “lean Republican” heading into Tuesday.

Huizenga, an eight-term congressman and the committee’s vice chair, is the highest-ranking Republican on the panel to lose. He is not the only crypto ally on it to go down.

Rep. Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, who chairs the Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Artificial Intelligence, lost to Democrat Mitchell Berman 52% to 48%. The AP called that race at 11:48 p.m. Tuesday.

Rep. Ann Wagner of Missouri, who chairs the capital markets subcommittee, lost to Democrat Fred Wellman. Rep. Zach Nunn of Iowa lost to state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott, and Rep. Mike Lawler of New York conceded to Democrat Cait Conley before the AP called his race.

Fairshake’s $1 million bets come up short

Fairshake committed at least $1 million in October to each of six House incumbents, among them Huizenga, Steil and committee Chairman French Hill of Arkansas. The super PAC reported spending $1,019,166 to support Huizenga in the general election, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

All 32 House incumbents the Fairshake network backed this fall voted for the CLARITY Act when it passed the House 294-134 in July 2025, CNBC reported. The network entered September with about $120.4 million in cash.

The crypto money was a small slice of the Huizenga race. Outside groups reported more than $25 million in spending in the district, FEC filings show, with House Majority PAC alone putting about $6 million against the Republican.

Two of Fairshake’s three Republican $1 million picks on the committee have now lost in midterms. Hill’s own race had not been called by the AP as of Wednesday afternoon. He led Democrat Chris Jones by about 4,400 votes, or 50.9% to 49.1%, with 99% of the expected vote counted.

What the losses mean for crypto in the House

Democrats won control of the House on Tuesday, which hands the committee gavel to their side regardless of Hill’s result. Rep. Maxine Waters of California, the panel’s top Democrat and its chair from 2019 to 2023, is in line to return to the post. Nineteen Financial Services Democrats backed her in October against a possible challenge from Rep. Sean Casten of Illinois, Politico reported.

Steil’s loss also leaves the digital assets subcommittee without its chair. Huizenga sat on that panel too. Journalist Eleanor Terrett noted that the subcommittee’s name, scope and membership are set each Congress, so Democrats could rename, re-scope or eliminate it.

Huizenga played a role in moving the stablecoin bill President Donald Trump signed in 2025, and he led the committee’s investigations into former SEC Chair Gary Gensler during the Biden administration.

The industry’s main legislative goal is still the CLARITY Act, which failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. House Democrats are already weighing their own market structure bill with a bigger role for the SEC.

Crypto groups spent heavily to avoid this outcome, with about $176 million committed to more than 100 races this cycle. Losing Huizenga and Steil removes two of the Republicans who shaped crypto legislation on the committee, and both seats flip to Democrats.

Bitcoin itself rallied after the Democratic sweep, even as the industry’s allies in Congress lost ground.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: French Bank Credit Mutuel Arkea Confirms Cyberattack as ZachXBT Puts Losses Above $133 Million
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

French Bank Credit Mutuel Arkea Confirms Cyberattack as ZachXBT Puts Losses Above $133 Million
Credit Mutuel Arkea says a cyberattack through a service provider enabled fraudulent transfers from its own account, while ZachXBT puts the theft above $133 million, a figure the bank has...
content:
French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea said Wednesday that a cyberattack allowed hackers to carry out fraudulent transfers from the bank’s own account, a theft that on-chain investigator ZachXBT has put at more than $133 million and that the bank has not confirmed.

The Brittany-based lender said in a statement that the incident was under control, that operations were resuming and that customer assets were not affected. It suspended some transactions as a precaution.

“This incident has had no impact on (customer) assets and has only caused a delay in the execution of certain transfers,” the bank said on its website, in a translation published by Reuters.

In a follow-up question-and-answer note, Credit Mutuel Arkea said the attackers went through the platform of one of its service providers and reached the bank directly. They used the bank’s own account to send transactions to other banks, which then potentially allowed them to convert the money into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms, the bank said.

No customer accounts at its federations or subsidiaries were used, the bank said. It denied French press reports that the attackers got in through Fortuneo, its online banking arm, and said the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack was “a sophisticated attack from the outside,” not the result of human error.

The size of the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack

The bank has not given a final figure. Asked whether 118 million euros, or $133 million, had been stolen, it said it does not confirm the number and can only “validate the order of magnitude.”

Part of the funds involved has been frozen and other steps are underway to recover the rest, the bank said. It added that the amounts at stake are “absolutely not” large enough to threaten its financial health or soundness.

AFP reported that the bank put the attack at about 100 million euros in a provisional estimate. Earlier Wednesday, Reuters reported that the bank said its losses were lower than $133 million. “It is still too early to give a final figure,” a spokesperson told the wire service.

What ZachXBT reported

ZachXBT first flagged the incident on Monday without naming the victim. He wrote on his Telegram channel that an EU entity was suspected of losing more than $106 million from multiple centralized exchange accounts on Nov. 1, with the funds withdrawn as USDC and USDT. He said the funds were then swapped for ether and moved across several chains.

In an update, he said he had found another $27 million or more in exchange withdrawals, bringing the total to more than $133 million. A later post named Credit Mutuel Arkea as the alleged victim. He wrote that the attack “occurred for multiple days” and that he suspects the amount stolen is larger once over-the-counter activity is counted.

The bank has not confirmed his figure or his timeline. It has also not said when the attack began, who was behind it or whether any data was taken. Credit Mutuel Arkea is working with judicial and police authorities to determine the origin of the attack and how it was carried out. It said it informed its supervisors once the attack was detected.

The bank also warned customers that phishing attempts are possible after the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack.

Credit Mutuel Arkea, which groups the Credit Mutuel federations of Brittany and the Southwest, is part of the wider Credit Mutuel group. It has 5.8 million clients and 211.5 billion euros, or about $238 billion, in assets, Reuters reported. It posted net profit of 230 million euros in the first half of the year, AFP reported.

The Credit Mutuel Arkea hack lands less than a week after the record $6.34 billion Binance hack, which blockchain analysis firms have linked to North Korea. ZachXBT said in his first post that he was highly confident this incident was not the work of North Korea’s Lazarus Group. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin also froze deposits and withdrawals this week after a security incident.

How much of the money the bank can recover, and what the final loss from the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack will be, remains open.

Micah Zimmerman
