title: House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With a Bigger SEC Role After Sweep
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With a Bigger SEC Role After Sweep
House Democrats are discussing a crypto market structure bill built on Rep. Maxine Waters' rejected Clarity Act amendments, with a bigger SEC role, a smaller CFTC role and new ethics limit...
content:
House Democrats are discussing a plan to turn Rep. Maxine Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own crypto market structure bill next Congress, with ideas that include a bigger role for the SEC and a smaller one for the CFTC, Eleanor Terrett reported Wednesday.

The proposal would fold in the Democratic Clarity Act provisions Waters offered in the House, which were not adopted, plus the provisions Senate Democrats were able to agree on with Republicans before September’s failed cloture vote. Terrett cited three industry sources who have spoken with Democratic staffers.

Further ethics provisions restricting the crypto activities of President Donald Trump and other federal officials are also likely, she wrote. Republicans are calling it a “messaging bill.”

No text for the crypto market structure bill has been released, and the details so far come from industry sources rather than from lawmakers.

The talks follow Tuesday’s Democratic sweep of Congress. Waters, the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, is in line to take the gavel in January from Chairman French Hill, the Clarity Act’s sponsor.

Bloomberg Law reported Wednesday that the new majorities give Democrats leverage over the Clarity Act, the industry’s top legislative priority, starting with tougher ethics rules aimed at Trump’s ventures.

What the Waters amendment would do for crypto

Waters offered the bill of rights as amendment #31 to H.R. 3633 in July 2025. The House Rules Committee blocked it 4-8 along party lines, on a motion from Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon of Pennsylvania. Making an amendment “in order” lets the full House debate and vote on it, so the result kept the package off the floor.

The committee’s record lists what it would have required: 24/7 customer service, insurance or SIPC-like coverage, fiduciary and best-execution rules, anti-front-running rules, bankruptcy-remote custody with 24-hour withdrawals and monthly auditor-attested proof of reserves. It would also have sent more funding to the SEC and CFTC.

The committee rejected a second Democratic amendment by the same 4-8 margin. That one, from Rep. Joe Neguse of Colorado, would have barred members of Congress, presidents and vice presidents from issuing or endorsing digital assets. The ethics fight it previewed later followed the bill to the Senate.

SEC versus CFTC

The agency split is where a Democratic crypto market structure bill would break most sharply from the Republican one. The House-passed Clarity Act directs the CFTC to regulate most digital commodity trading, including exchanges, brokers and dealers, and exempts tokens on mature blockchains from SEC registration under certain conditions.

That design is the one the industry backed. A crypto market structure bill that moves supervision back toward the SEC would reverse it.

The Clarity Act passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. Sen. Thom Tillis entered a motion to reconsider, which preserves the option of another vote, but the bill dies when this Congress ends on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

Democrats now hold the leverage. “The industry and the Republicans screwed up. That was the best bill they were going to get,” Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, a Senate Banking Committee member, said in comments reported by Bloomberg Law.

TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg wrote Wednesday that the sweep closes the door on Clarity for two years, and that Democratic investigations of the Trump family’s crypto ventures “may make it impossible to advance a version of Clarity that the crypto sector could back.”

A Democratic crypto market structure bill would still need Trump’s signature to become law. Whether one built around the SEC can draw enough Republican votes to get there, or remains the messaging bill Republicans say it is, is the question the next Congress opens with.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $80,000 as Democratic Sweep Sparks Short Squeeze
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Holds Near $80,000 as Democratic Sweep Sparks Short Squeeze
Bitcoin price holds near $80,000 after rebounding from an election-night low of $75,600, as a short squeeze, a stock rally and a 9% drop in oil follow the Democratic sweep of Congress.
This post Bitcoin Price...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $80,000 on Wednesday afternoon, up about 3% on the day and roughly $26,000 below its price one year ago, as markets shook off election-night jitters over the Democratic sweep of Congress, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data.

Bitcoin changed hands at $80,099 at 3:12 p.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.61 trillion and roughly $39.6 billion in trading volume over the past 24 hours.

The low came in the 10 p.m. ET hour on Tuesday, as results showed Democrats taking both chambers. The high came in the 10 a.m. hour on Wednesday. That is a swing of about 7.3% from bottom to top in roughly 12 hours.

The climb was a short squeeze. About $950 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and bets against prices made up $560 million of that. Bitcoin positions accounted for $403 million of the total, 76% of it shorts.

CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju wrote on X Wednesday afternoon that $215 million in bitcoin shorts were liquidated in a single hour.

The view among analysts is that the sell-off had already done its work. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the sweep was largely priced into bitcoin before the vote, leaving room for a relief rally once the uncertainty cleared.

Lumida CEO Ram Ahluwalia had laid out the same path in a podcast interview the day before the election. A Democratic sweep, he said, would bring “a one and done washout, and that resets where asset prices are.”

Stocks, oil and a weaker dollar

Bitcoin price did not rally alone. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 1,500 points, or 3%, on Wednesday afternoon, while the S&P 500 climbed 1.7% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.8%. Apple and Microsoft touched record highs.

Oil moved the most. Brent crude fell more than 9% to $93.91 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropped nearly 9% to $87.59 by 12:36 p.m. ET, CNBC reported, after Vice President JD Vance blamed the Republican losses on the Iran war.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote on X.

That matters for bitcoin price because crude above $100 has kept inflation hot and the Federal Reserve leaning toward a December hike. The U.S. dollar index fell 0.55% to 101.32 in early trading, its lowest since Oct. 1.

What comes next for bitcoin price

Demand from funds has not caught up with the price. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $115.6 million on Tuesday, their third straight session of outflows, with BlackRock’s IBIT losing $95 million. The three-day total comes to about $1.16 billion. Wednesday’s flows will be reported after the U.S. close.

The policy picture got worse for the industry, not better. TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg wrote that the sweep makes a crypto-backed CLARITY Act “impossible,” and the committees that oversee crypto pass to Democrats in January.

On-chain analysts frame the move as a retest. Glassnode said in its Week on Chain report that the bitcoin price is testing the levels it broke above in August, with the True Market Mean at $77,700 and the short-term holder cost basis at $75,700. Holding above them, the firm wrote, keeps the August uptrend in place.

The calendar stays busy. The October jobs report lands Friday, October CPI follows on Nov. 10 and the Fed’s next decision comes on Dec. 9, as noted in Tuesday’s preview. Bitcoin price remains about 36% below its all-time high near $126,080.

The test now is whether ETF buyers return to carry the price once the shorts are gone. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $80,200.

Micah Zimmerman

title: Bitcoin Miner Riot Platforms Sells $750M in BTC as Hut 8 Dumps $250M
summary: Bitcoin mining companies Riot Platforms and Hut 8 disclosed substantial bitcoin sales in their respective third-quarter earnings reports on Wednesday, with Riot liquidating more than 10,000 BTC during the quarter to finance its data center expansion and Hut 8 selling cryptocurrency to fund share rep...
content:
Bitcoin mining companies Riot Platforms and Hut 8 disclosed substantial bitcoin sales in their respective third-quarter earnings reports on Wednesday, with Riot liquidating more than 10,000 BTC during the quarter to finance its data center expansion and Hut 8 selling cryptocurrency to fund share repurchases.

Key Takeaways

  • Riot Platforms sold 10,599 BTC for $751.5 million in Q3, bringing its 2026 sales to 20,264 BTC worth nearly $1.5 billion, as it shifts capital toward AI and data center infrastructure.
  • Hut 8 sold 954 BTC for $74.8 million in Q3 to fund share buybacks, followed by another 2,148 BTC for $175.4 million in October, totaling approximately $250 million in sales across both periods.
  • Both miners reported mixed quarterly results: Riot generated $181.4 million in revenue and $4 million in net income, while Hut 8 posted $71.1 million in revenue and $131.1 million in net income, with both advancing major AI infrastructure projects.

Bitcoin Miners Part With Holdings

Riot sold 10,599 BTC for approximately $751.5 million during the three months ended Sept. 30, accounting for more than half of the 20,264 BTC it has sold so far this year. The company generated nearly $1.5 billion from those sales over the first nine months of 2026, dramatically reducing its bitcoin reserves as it builds infrastructure for artificial intelligence computing.

The third-quarter sales accelerated from 5,887 BTC sold for approximately $443 million in the second quarter and 3,778 BTC sold for $289.5 million in the first quarter. Riot ended September holding just 2,418 BTC, down from 18,005 BTC at the beginning of the year.

Hut 8, meanwhile, sold approximately 954 BTC for $74.8 million during the third quarter to finance stock repurchases. The company subsequently sold another 2,148 BTC for $175.4 million in October, bringing its combined sales across the two periods to 3,102 BTC worth approximately $250.2 million.

Unlike Riot, Hut 8 did not report comparable cash bitcoin sales during the first two quarters of 2026. Its earlier digital asset activity included bitcoin purchases and transfers to settle mining equipment obligations.

The two companies’ sales underscore differing strategies for deploying their cryptocurrency reserves, with Riot directing proceeds toward infrastructure development while Hut 8 uses bitcoin holdings to return capital to shareholders.

Riot reported third-quarter revenue of $181.4 million, up 1% from $180.2 million a year earlier. Bitcoin mining revenue declined to $116 million from $160.8 million, despite production increasing 16% to 1,637 BTC. Revenue from data centers reached $18.4 million, while engineering revenue climbed to $47 million.

The company posted net income of approximately $4 million, compared with $104.5 million a year earlier. It ended September with $950.2 million in cash and bitcoin, and said it had not raised equity capital during 2026.

Next Moves for Riot, Hut 8

Riot also announced a 15-year lease covering 910 megawatts of computing capacity at its Corsicana, Texas, facility, valued at approximately $28 billion over the initial term. Including other agreements, the company now has approximately $38 billion in contracted data center revenue.

Hut 8 reported third-quarter revenue of $71.1 million, down from $83.5 million a year earlier, while net income attributable to the company increased to $131.1 million from $50.1 million. Its quarterly results benefited from a substantial noncash gain related to the rising value of its digital assets.

The company reported holding 16,787 BTC across its consolidated operations at the end of September, valued at approximately $1.4 billion, including holdings associated with its majority-owned, Trump family-backed American Bitcoin subsidiary.

Hut 8 also highlighted progress on its AI infrastructure expansion, including the commercialization of its Beacon Point campus and the advancement of 1,300 megawatts of energy capacity into exclusive development discussions. It secured a $1.07 billion revolving credit facility and expanded its stock repurchase authorization to $1 billion following the quarter’s end.

Riot’s quarterly filing indicates that its bitcoin sales may continue. The company said it expects to sell substantially all newly mined bitcoin to finance development and operating expenses rather than rebuild a sizable cryptocurrency treasury.

The firms have seen vastly different market reactions to their respective earnings reports on Wednesday, with Riot (RIOT) shares rising over12% to recently trade at $15.75, while Hut 8 (HUT) shares have plunged more than 21% to a recent price of $50.06.

title: Gold Price Forecast Faces December Fed Test as $3,900 Support Comes Into View
summary: As gold prices retreat from $4,000, the safety index is coming.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

As gold prices retreat from $4,000, the safety index is coming.

The December Fed decision could be the turning point for bullion to rally or continue its drop at the end of the year, with sellers pushing toward $3,900 support.

Gold Price Analysis Shows Sellers Still Control the Trend

Gold is struggling to be bullish in November trading below a key area near the $4,000 mark. Investing.com’s November 3 chart showed gold futures at $3,946.85, down $22.75, or 0.57%. Meanwhile, the TradingView chart shows spot gold trading at $3,935.13 on the current four-hour candle, down 0.24%. These are independent instruments, and their prices ought not to be compared.

Gold has been chopping around a bit in the $4600 range since its August recovery, with a series of lower highs and lower lows on the four-hour chart. Source: TradingView

The sales pressure then drove prices back to $3,900. The liquidity heatmap shows a cluster of potential resistance at around 4,200-4,600 and a large liquidity zone around 3,800-3,900. These zones are used to show zones that traders can watch for, not certain turning points.

In the near term, 3,900–3,880 is the key support area. A break below will open $3,800 and possibly the $3,700s. But gold has to clear 3,975-4,000 before bulls can put up a fight at $4,044 and begin the recovery. Any move above these areas would be a positive development technically, but the overall downtrend would need to be confirmed.

December Fed Decision Could Determine Gold’s Direction

The Fed kept interest rates steady at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28, with two members wanting to raise rates by a quarter point. The Fed also indicated that inflation continues to be high. The disagreement puts investors on edge about the possibility of a further contraction by policymakers at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. Read the official Fed statement and 2026 meeting calendar.

A rate increase or hawkish sentiment may extend the downward trend for gold as it helps to lift Treasury yields and the US dollar. The larger the crop, the greater the opportunity cost of carrying non-yielding bullion.

But if the inflation report is less severe and the employment report comes in light, or the Fed outlook is less hawkish, then rate expectations will be lowered, bringing gold back. Investors will need to monitor upcoming U.S. inflation and jobs data, as well as the dollar and real yields, rather than rely on the Fed’s decision to move prices.

Can Gold Rally in November and December?

There is still a chance that it will be able to make a decent rally, but the charts do not confirm one just yet. Gold must drink this resistance at 3,880–3,900; if it can cut through, it will recover $4,000 and break through on and off the resistance levels. In November, if those conditions persist and yields continue to drop, MBLIO investment demand could increase; a $4,044 or higher resistance may emerge. Lack of support to be found would instead continue the bear case for December.

Central-bank demand could be a source of demand in the longer term, and geopolitical risks could drive safe-haven buying. However, neither of these is a sure sign of recovery. Rather than just buying when gold has dropped significantly, investors should think about entering gradually, setting positions, and predetermined exit points.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What’s the important price level for gold?

The immediate support zone is 3,900–3,880. If it falls below and continues to do so, $3,800 will be left vulnerable.

2. Will $4,000 be the minimum price for gold by November?

Yes, if the buyer supports and recovers $4,000. The recovery must be confirmed above $4,044 to support a stronger recovery.

3. What is the likely impact of the Fed on gold in December?

Hawkish policy sentiment and higher rates could weigh on gold, while dovish policy sentiment and lower yields could work in favor of gold.

4. Should you invest in gold now?

It is dependent on risk-taking capability and investment time horizon. It is better to be prudent rather than assuming a bottom, as it is currently in a downtrend.

title: Trump-linked tokens lead crypto losses after Democrats sweep in the US midterms
summary: The official Trump and World Liberty Financial tokens were the two biggest losers among the top 100 cryptocurrencies on Wednesday, even as Bitcoin and Ether rallied.
content:
Two crypto tokens linked to US President Donald Trump led losses among the top 100 digital assets on Wednesday following the US midterm elections, raising questions about their future as the broader crypto market rallied.

Official Trump (TRUMP) fell 17% over 24 hours to $1.33, while World Liberty Financial (WLFI) dropped over 7% to $0.047, according to CoinMarketCap data from around 5:32 pm UTC. TRUMP is the president’s official memecoin, launched in January 2025, while WLFI is the governance token of World Liberty Financial, a Trump family-backed decentralized finance (DeFi) project launched in 2024.

The declines followed a wave of Democratic victories, including surprise wins in Texas, in Tuesday’s midterm elections, with the party winning control of both the House and Senate from Republicans.

The results could not only make it harder for Trump to push forward his crypto plans but also bring more scrutiny to his family’s crypto businesses. Analysts say the losses also raise questions about whether political sentiment alone can fuel demand for Trump-linked tokens.

Political tokens slide while Bitcoin, Ether rally

Bitcoin (BTC) rose more than 4% over 24 hours to around $80,500, while Ether (ETH) climbed 6% to $2,433, according to CoinMarketCap data. Other major cryptocurrencies also posted gains, with BNB rising 3%, XRP climbing 2.6% and Solana (SOL) gaining 2.5%. The overall crypto market rose 3.4% to $2.69 trillion.

Meanwhile, the losses extended to other Trump family-linked tokens, such as the MELANIA memecoin, associated with First Lady Melania Trump. MELANIA dropped nearly 13% over 24 hours to around $0.066.

A separate token named after Vice President JD Vance (VANCE) also dropped nearly 12%, although it has no confirmed official connection to the vice president.

The losses were further reflected across the broader political memecoin market, with the sector’s total market capitalization falling more than 16% on the day to $477 million. Trading volume jumped 123% to $437 million, per CoinMarketCap data.

Related: US midterm elections 2026 as it happened: Democrats win control of Congress

A growing divergence raises lingering questions

Benjamin Sarquis Peillard, founder and CEO of Cap, a DeFi platform focused on stablecoin yields, told Cointelegraph that investors appear to be treating politically linked tokens differently from other cryptocurrencies.

“Bitcoin and other established assets respond to a combination of liquidity, institutional flows and macroeconomic conditions, while politically linked tokens can be more sensitive to shifts in expectations around Washington,” he said. “Even as the broader market recovers, those tokens may face selling pressure if investors begin reassessing their risk exposure.”

And while the selloff could be indicative of a short-term reaction to the election results, Peillard said the “longer-term question is what supports demand for these tokens beyond their association with a political figure.”

The CLARITY Act and beyond

Beyond the market reaction, the election results also raise questions about the future of US crypto legislation, including the currently stalled Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, commonly referred to as the CLARITY Act.

The bill, which aims to establish a regulatory framework for digital assets, failed to advance in the Senate earlier this year after falling short of the 60 votes required. Democrats were pushing for stronger ethical provisions and safeguards against conflicts of interest involving Trump’s crypto ventures — four Republicans also opposed advancing the legislation.

“The midterm results introduce a new layer of regulatory uncertainty, particularly around the pace and direction of digital asset legislation,” Peillard said. “For politically linked tokens, that uncertainty can have a more immediate impact because investor sentiment is partly tied to expectations around the political environment.”

While the crypto sector continues to have support — and opposition — from lawmakers in both parties, it remains to be seen how the election results will affect crypto legislation.

Peillard said that for the broader industry, the “more important question is whether Congress can establish a durable regulatory framework that provides clarity regardless of which party holds power.”

title: Riot shares surge on $28B AI lease as Hut 8 sinks on revenue miss
summary: Bitcoin miner Riot sold BTC to finance its AI expansion, while Hut 8 reported falling revenue and rising costs before its major data center leases generate income.
content:
Shares of Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms surged more than 13% Wednesday after the company announced a $28 billion AI data center lease, its largest agreement to date as it accelerates its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The 15-year agreement covers 910 megawatts at its Corsicana, Texas, facility, bringing its total future contracted data center revenue to approximately $38 billion across three leases signed this year. The agreement represents a major step in Riot’s AI infrastructure strategy as it moves away from relying primarily on Bitcoin mining revenue.

“A year ago, our cash flow depended on the price of Bitcoin, and now, at full deployment of currently executed deals, nearly all of our expected cash flow will be generated from long-term leases with leading players in the AI ecosystem,” CEO Jason Les said during Wednesday’s earnings call.

Source: Yahoo Finance

According to Riot’s third-quarter earnings release, Riot will provide land and power infrastructure originally developed for Bitcoin mining, while the AI tenant, identified as Anthropic in the company’s quarterly filing, will own and operate the computing equipment and cover operating expenses.

Riot estimates the project’s total capital costs at $5.5 billion, financed primarily through debt backed by lease payments, although financing has not yet been secured. The first phase is expected to be delivered in September 2027, with rental payments beginning within 60 days of delivery.

Riot also reported third-quarter revenue of $181.4 million, up just 1% year over year, and sold 10,599 BTC during the quarter to help finance its data center expansion. During Wednesday’s earnings call, CEO Jason Les said Bitcoin mining at Corsicana could begin winding down in summer 2027.

Related: Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals 

Hut 8 shares tumble as AI transition weighs on revenue

Meanwhile, shares of fellow Bitcoin miner Hut 8 plunged more than 22% at one point on Wednesday after the company reported weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue amid its transition toward AI infrastructure.

Third-quarter revenue fell 15% to $71.1 million, missing analysts’ estimates of $75.8 million, according to MarketBeat data. During Wednesday’s earnings call, CFO Sean Glennan attributed the decline partly to asset sales and lower revenue per Bitcoin mined, while cash administrative expenses also rose year over year.

“The legacy revenue base is no longer the main growth driver, while the larger contracted infrastructure revenues remain tied to delivery milestones,” Glennan said.

Source: Yahoo Finance

CEO Asher Genoot also pointed to the complexity and expense of traditional AI data center construction as the company looks to develop projects on a larger scale.

“Many of today’s data centers resemble NASA rocket programs—remarkable engineering, but complex, expensive, and slow to deliver,” Genoot said.

According to the company’s third-quarter earnings presentation, Hut 8 has already secured $7.5 billion in project bonds to fully finance two major AI data center developments, although neither has begun generating lease revenue.

title: Italy Filed 95% of the EU's Register of Unlicensed Crypto Firms
summary:
Italy's market regulator filed 179 of the 188 entries on the EU's register of unlicensed crypto firms, an FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows. Authorities in four other countries supplied the remaining nine.
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) keeps the list u...
content:
2026-11-04T20:39:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 04/11/2026 | 18:39 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • CONSOB sent 179 of 188 entries. Germany, home to the most licensed providers, sent none.
  • BaFin issued 89 warnings mentioning crypto this year, and none reached the ESMA file.

Italy's market regulator filed 179 of the 188 entries on the EU's register of unlicensed crypto firms, an FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows. Authorities in four other countries supplied the remaining nine.

The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA ) keeps the list under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The law's transition period ended on July 1 for providers without a license.

It is the only EU-wide public record of firms that national supervisors say serve clients without authorization, and it is mostly a record of one supervisor's work.

Banks, payment firms and brokers that screen counterparties against it draw on five of the 30 European Economic Area (EEA) states, according to FM Intelligence's review of ESMA's October 29 file.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Italy's Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa (CONSOB) has ordered internet providers to black out unauthorized financial websites since 2019. Its tally reached 1,861 sites on October 29, 250 of them tied to crypto-assets, according to the regulator.

A supervisor that already names domains in bulk may find it easier to pass them on to ESMA, the analysis said.

Germany Leads on Licenses and Files No Entries

Germany sits at the other end. ESMA lists 119 authorized or notified providers based there, the most of any member state, as it was when FM Intelligence mapped the register in August. Most of them are banks and investment firms notified under MiCA.

German supervisors have filed no entry in the non-compliant register. At home, the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) published 245 consumer warnings in 2026 to November 3, and 89 of them mention crypto services, FM Intelligence's Fines & Warnings Tracker shows.

The same split appears wherever national warning lists are busy. France's Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) said on October 19 it had added 64 crypto names to its own blacklist since January.

The Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC ) cited MiCA's Article 59 in its September website warnings, and again in October. Neither authority has an entry in the ESMA file.

The rest of the file comes from four authorities. Belgium's Financial Services and Markets Authority filed six entries and the Czech, Dutch and Slovak authorities one each, which leaves 25 EEA states with none.

Nothing Obliges Supervisors to File

MiCA's Article 110 describes the register as non-exhaustive. It sets the minimum content of an entry but no duty or deadline for national authorities to submit one. Many German and French warnings also cover mixed investment and crypto offers that fall under national banking or securities law.

Germany's zero is therefore consistent with a different reporting channel rather than an absence of unlicensed crypto offers, the analysis concluded.

The gap sits beside a separate debate over who supervises crypto firms. EU finance ministers agreed on October 9 to limit direct ESMA supervision to the largest cross-border providers, narrowing a European Commission plan to move all of them to the Paris-based authority.

A BaFin executive director said in September that firms choose Europe's weakest supervisor and then expand across the bloc.

Central supervision would address where firms are licensed. The ESMA file points to a second gap, in where unlicensed activity is reported, and ESMA has added no entry of its own.

The full FM Intelligence analysis examines what the 188 entries contain, a detail that limits their use in counterparty screening, and projects the size of the file by June 30, 2027, when the Commission is due to report on MiCA.

Italy's Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa (CONSOB) has ordered internet providers to black out unauthorized financial websites since 2019. Its tally reached 1,861 sites on October 29, 250 of them tied to crypto-assets, according to the regulator.

A supervisor that already names domains in bulk may find it easier to pass them on to ESMA, the analysis said.

Germany Leads on Licenses and Files No Entries

Germany sits at the other end. ESMA lists 119 authorized or notified providers based there, the most of any member state, as it was when FM Intelligence mapped the register in August. Most of them are banks and investment firms notified under MiCA.

German supervisors have filed no entry in the non-compliant register. At home, the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) published 245 consumer warnings in 2026 to November 3, and 89 of them mention crypto services, FM Intelligence's Fines & Warnings Tracker shows.

The same split appears wherever national warning lists are busy. France's Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) said on October 19 it had added 64 crypto names to its own blacklist since January.

The Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC ) cited MiCA's Article 59 in its September website warnings, and again in October. Neither authority has an entry in the ESMA file.

The rest of the file comes from four authorities. Belgium's Financial Services and Markets Authority filed six entries and the Czech, Dutch and Slovak authorities one each, which leaves 25 EEA states with none.

Nothing Obliges Supervisors to File

MiCA's Article 110 describes the register as non-exhaustive. It sets the minimum content of an entry but no duty or deadline for national authorities to submit one. Many German and French warnings also cover mixed investment and crypto offers that fall under national banking or securities law.

Germany's zero is therefore consistent with a different reporting channel rather than an absence of unlicensed crypto offers, the analysis concluded.

The gap sits beside a separate debate over who supervises crypto firms. EU finance ministers agreed on October 9 to limit direct ESMA supervision to the largest cross-border providers, narrowing a European Commission plan to move all of them to the Paris-based authority.

A BaFin executive director said in September that firms choose Europe's weakest supervisor and then expand across the bloc.

Central supervision would address where firms are licensed. The ESMA file points to a second gap, in where unlicensed activity is reported, and ESMA has added no entry of its own.

The full FM Intelligence analysis examines what the 188 entries contain, a detail that limits their use in counterparty screening, and projects the size of the file by June 30, 2027, when the Commission is due to report on MiCA.

title: Matt Corallo Flags Critical Linux Kernel Flaw; Lightning Labs Ships LND Mitigation
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Matt Corallo Flags Critical Linux Kernel Flaw; Lightning Labs Ships LND Mitigation
Bitcoin Core and Lightning developer Matt Corallo highlighted CVE-2026-98432 on October 30, a use-after-free in the Linux kernel IPv4 TCP handshake code scored CVSS 9.8. Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team...
content:
Bitcoin Core and Lightning developer Matt Corallo highlighted a severe Linux kernel vulnerability on October 30, criticizing Ubuntu’s delayed response to what he called “the most critical Linux vuln ever.” The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects the kernel’s IPv4 TCP handshake code with a CVSS severity score of 9.8. Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team later showed it could be turned into a remote root exploit against systems exposing a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener.

Peter Todd echoed the warning the same day, advising anyone running LND on Linux with open ports to shut their Bitcoin Lightning nodes down until the kernel was patched or otherwise mitigated. The demonstrated exploit path relies on an MPTCP listener—something Go 1.24 and later enable by default. Because LND is written in Go, recent versions were listening with MPTCP on their peer, gRPC, and REST ports whenever the kernel had the feature enabled.

Lightning Labs responded the same day with emergency releases: lnd v0.21.6-beta and the backport v0.20.7-beta. Both disable MPTCP listeners by default, closing the demonstrated exploit path through LND. The project described the change as a mitigation, not a fix, and noted that only a patched kernel fully resolves the underlying issue. Other services on the same machine remain exposed until MPTCP is disabled host-wide or the kernel is updated. Olaoluwa Osuntokun and the official Lightning Labs account both recommended the update.

Security researcher Marcus Hutchins later reported internet-wide scanning activity consistent with threat actors looking for exposed systems. His scans found roughly 2.1 million servers reachable over MPTCP on port 443. International Cyber Digest amplified the finding on November 4, noting the scanning and Ubuntu’s slower patch timeline. 

Canonical has since made fixed kernels available in the opt-in, proposed pocket for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04, but they have not yet reached the regular updates channel. Red Hat shipped fixes for RHEL 8/9/10 on November 1; Debian, Amazon Linux, and others had already released patches earlier.

UmbrelOS 2.0.1 included the kernel fix on November 1st for x86 devices and applied a traffic-blocking mitigation on Raspberry Pi, where a fixed kernel was not yet available. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation has been reported, and the vulnerability has not been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Anthropic’s remote-root demonstration remains unpublished.

The practical exposure is highest on internet-facing servers. Home desktop systems behind typical NAT and firewalls, without public TCP listeners, are far less affected. For Lightning operators on Linux, the LND releases remove the specific MPTCP listener path the public exploit used, but the broader kernel bug remains until a patched kernel is installed.

title: Strategy’s STRC Hits $100 Par for First Time Since May After Over $2 Billion in Buybacks
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy’s STRC Hits $100 Par for First Time Since May After Over $2 Billion in Buybacks
Strategy’s STRC preferred hit $100 par on Wednesday for the first time since May, after billions in buybacks, a 12% dividend rate and a switch to daily payouts.
This post Strategy’s STRC Hits $...
content:
Strategy’s Stretch preferred stock touched $100 today for the first time since May, returning to the par value the company has spent over $2 billion in buybacks and five months of rate increases to defend.

STRC traded below $80 at times in June, a massive discount to its stated value. The climb back to $100 restores the price at which Strategy says it will resume issuing new shares, the mechanism that funds its bitcoin purchases. Chairman Michael Saylor had pledged to keep the stock at or above par and to hold the dividend at 12% until it got there.

Two changes landed in the past week. Shareholders approved daily dividends on STRC and three other preferreds on Oct. 28 by a 99.3% vote, removing the semi-monthly ex-dividend drops that had added volatility to the price. 

The first daily payment went out Monday. And Strategy’s Oct. 29 filing set the November rate at 12% annualized, or $1 per share for the month.

Shares of Strategy (MSTR) were up over 7% today after bitcoin jumped above $80,000.

What Stretch (STRC) is and why it slipped

Stretch, the Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred, launched in July 2025 at $90 with a 9% starting rate. Saylor called it the company’s “iPhone moment.” The design is a feedback loop: Strategy adjusts the dividend each month to hold the price near $100, sells new shares when it trades above par and uses the cash to buy bitcoin. 

It became the largest tradable preferred in the world, with a market value above $8 billion and a holder base that CEO Phong Le has put at about 80% retail.

The loop broke earlier this year. STRC drifted below par in late January; Strategy raised the rate to 11.25% in February, 11.5% in March and 12% by summer, and the price kept sliding as bitcoin fell toward $65,000. At $89 the at-the-market program sat idle, cutting off the company’s cheapest funding. 

In late May, Strategy sold 32 BTC for about $2.5 million to cover a Stretch distribution, its first bitcoin sale since 2022, and critics raised the prospect of a “death spiral” that analysts at Benchmark and TD Cowen disputed.

The fix was to buy the stock back. Strategy paused bitcoin purchases in the week of Oct. 19 and spent $204.9 million on STRC alone, part of the roughly $2.25 billion it has retired since the discount opened. 

Each share bought below $100 shrank the float and reduced the dividend bill at the same time.

A thin cushion under the treasury

The recovery matters because of what sits beneath it. Strategy holds 849,327 BTC after adding 811 coins last week, at an average cost of about $75,446. With bitcoin near $78,300 on Wednesday, the position is about 4% above water. 

The company reported $20.91 billion in third-quarter operating income, almost all of it unrealized gains, alongside a negative year-to-date BTC yield and a chief financial officer stepping down.

The preferred stack is the bill that comes due regardless. STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD together carry annual dividends in the hundreds of millions, and the quarter’s 5,552 BTC in sales went to fund them and the buybacks. A Stretch at par lets Strategy pay those obligations with new preferred issuance rather than coins. A Stretch at $89 does not.

The test now is whether the company reopens the ATM at $100 and whether buyers absorb it. 

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

content:

Wednesday, 04/11/2026 | 16:28 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Recently, Vantage, Blueberry Markets, BitDelta and Moneta Markets secured UAE Category 5 licences.
  • The licence allows the firm to introduce clients to affiliated trading firms, but not operate a brokerage.

BtcDana has secured a Category 5 licence from the UAE Capital Market Authority, allowing its local entity to conduct introduction and promotion activities.

London's trading industry is coming home!

BtcDana joins several international brokers that have obtained similar licences in the UAE. Vantage and Blueberry Markets received Category 5 approvals in July this year, followed by BitDelta later that month. Moneta Markets secured the same licence in August.

BtcDana Gets UAE Approval for Client Introductions

The licence falls under the CMA's Arrangement and Advice category. It allows BtcDana's UAE entity to promote financial services and introduce prospective clients to affiliated trading firms, but not to provide brokerage services or execute trades directly. The affiliated entities operate under their respective regulatory frameworks.

Peter Chow, Founder of BtcDana, said the licence provides the company with "a clearly defined framework for conducting Introduction and Promotion activities in the local market."

Founded in 2019, BtcDana says it serves more than 1.5 million active traders. Its platform offers more than 300 Contracts for Difference across forex , metals, indices and commodities, alongside mobile and desktop trading services.

The authorisation applies specifically to BtcDana's UAE entity and does not extend to its affiliated trading firms.

UAE CMA Reports 43% Licensing Growth

The CMA reported a 43% year-on-year increase in licensed companies in October. Its public register listed 28 firms authorised for over-the-counter derivatives and spot forex trading, up from 11 at the end of 2024.

The regulator also reported AED 1.2 billion in client refunds during the first nine months of 2026, compared with AED 8 million a year earlier. The figures were part of its first nine-month update since replacing the Securities and Commodities Authority on 1 January 2026.

content:
Website traffic and trading volumes can produce very different rankings among retail brokers, according to research discussed at the first Finance Magnates Intelligence Forum on September 30 at the Amara Hotel in Limassol, Cyprus.

The comparison highlights the limits of using website visits alone to assess a broker’s position in the retail trading market. Traffic can indicate how much attention a brand receives online, while trading volume provides a different measure of activity.

“Having the traffic means that you have the ability, the attention, let's say, of prospective traders. Having the trading volume means that you have the ability to convert, retain, so it doesn't necessarily mean the higher the traffic, the higher the trading volume,” Ramzi Ahmad, said.

The event brought together executives and specialists from the retail trading and financial services industries to discuss market data, regulation, growth and competitiveness.

Named speakers included Maciej Szeląg, CEE FinTech Lead at AWS; and Philios Petrides, Forex and Fintech Data Executive and BI Consultant; Neophytos Papageorgiou, CEO of Finance Magnates; Ahmad, Director of Intelligence at Finance Magnates; Demetris Koutsomichalis, Data Analyst at Finance Magnates.

Reported Trading Volumes Reach $50.7 Trillion

Separate data supplied by Finance Magnates Intelligence put reported broker trading volume at $50.7 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, up 94.2% from the first quarter.

The data also put the number of active trading accounts in the first half of 2026 at 19.4 million. The reported quarter-on-quarter growth rate for active accounts was 170%.

Finance Magnates Intelligence categorises its volume data as verified, reported or estimated. The $50.7 trillion figure falls into the reported category and should not be treated as a fully verified total for the entire retail trading market.

The data showed a change in the broker with the highest average monthly reported volume. TMGM led in the first quarter, with $2.1 trillion, while EC Markets led in the second quarter, with $2.2 trillion.

The confidence score attached to TMGM’s first-quarter figure was 95%, compared with 85% for EC Markets in the second quarter.

These figures cover trading volume and active accounts, while the ranking comparison discussed at the Forum examined the relationship between website traffic and trading volume. The measures provide different perspectives on broker activity and should not be treated as interchangeable.

Website Traffic Declines Across Major Regions

Separate regional traffic data supplied by Finance Magnates Intelligence showed declines across several major markets in the third quarter of 2026.

Europe accounted for 42% of the global share of voice tracked in the research, with 60.2 million organic users. The figure was down 32% from the previous quarter.

Asia-Pacific accounted for 30.5% of the tracked global share, with 43.8 million in organic traffic, down 33% quarter on quarter.

North America recorded the largest reported quarterly decline, at 59%. Latin America and Africa each accounted for 4.7% of the tracked global share, with declines of 14% and 13%, respectively. The Middle East and North Africa accounted for 4.1%, with 5.9 million organic users and a 30% quarterly decline.

Japan was the only market in the research to record quarter-on-quarter growth of more than 18.5%.

These figures describe website traffic and share of voice, rather than trading volume. The regional results show changes in online activity but do not, by themselves, establish corresponding changes in client deposits or trading activity.

Withdrawal Complaints Feature in Forum Discussion

Client withdrawals were another subject raised during the Forum.

One observation during the discussion was that withdrawal issues represented a large share of complaints tracked on social media.

“Two-thirds of all the complaints we've been tracking throughout the social media it's actually about withdrawals,” was noted during the executive discussions.

The discussion also raised questions about how brokers address withdrawal concerns in their public communications.

“But yet only two percent of the brokers that we've been tracking on our list show in the report that something about the withdrawals give some explanation.”

The two figures refer to different measures. The first concerns the share of complaints tracked on social media that relate to withdrawals. The second concerns the share of tracked brokers whose communications address withdrawals. They should not be interpreted as two measurements of the same thing.

The observations point to a difference between the issues raised by traders online and the subjects brokers address in their public-facing communications. The discussion did not establish whether these patterns apply equally across all brokers or complaint channels.

Data Quality and Broker Market Claims

The Forum also examined the challenges of comparing market data from different sources.

Data Analyst Demetris Koutsomichalis discussed the need to validate figures and ensure that information is linked to the correct broker, brand and legal entity.

“What’s hard is not finding data, is making sure it is actually correct, relevant and verifiable, and making sure the pieces connect and tell you a story.”

He also described how discrepancies between sources should be handled.

“When two sources disagree and sometimes they do, we don’t pick the more convenient number or take an average. We stop there and we go back to source.”

The discussion highlighted the importance of supporting market leadership claims with evidence.

“So be very careful when they say we are the biggest. That's a big question mark.”

Another comment challenged brokers to substantiate such claims.

“Okay, you're the biggest, show me the numbers.”

The traffic and volume comparison illustrates why the measure used to support a market position matters. A broker can attract substantial online attention without ranking first by trading volume, while a broker with high trading volume may attract less direct website traffic.

The role of introducing brokers and other partners in generating trading activity was also discussed. Such channels can bring clients to a broker without all of those clients first visiting its website. The ranking comparison alone, however, does not establish the contribution of each channel.

title: Binance Hacker Sends $798K in SOL to Privacy Cash, Laundering Spreads Across 11 Chains
summary:

The post Binance Hacker Sends $798K in SOL to Privacy Cash, Laundering Spre...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Binance hacker wallet deposited 8,567 SOL, or approximately $798,000, to Privacy Cash.
  • Elliptic mapped the laundering chain over approximately 12,000 wallets and 11 blockchains.
  • Approximately $3.18 billion of stolen crypto is in addresses related to the attack.

The laundering process is rapidly evolving for activities linked to Binance’s massive hack on Solana, with the stolen tokens now traveling through a privacy-focused mixer. Onchain Lens said a hacker-linked address deposited 8,567 SOL, valued at roughly $798,000, into Privacy Cash, while other related wallets showed similar activity.

BINANCE HACKER STARTS USING MIXER TO LAUNDER STOLEN FUNDS, MIXED 800K SO FAR ⚠️

An address linked to the hacker deposited 8,567 $SOL (~$798K) into Privacy Cash.

Multiple other addresses are showing similar activity. We are monitoring these movements in real time and working to trace and reconcile the full flow of funds.

@binance

— Onchain Lens (@OnchainLens) November 3, 2026

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Hacker Adds Privacy Cash to Laundering Route
  • SOL Is Being Split, Routed and Converted Into Bitcoin
    • Laundering Network Already Spans Thousands of Wallets
    • $3.18B in Stolen Crypto Still Remains Onchain

Binance Hacker Adds Privacy Cash to Laundering Route

The thefts of assets in Binance’s October 29 hack continue, with the Privacy Cash transfers as another development. Onchain Lens claims to be tracking the activity on stream and the work it is trying to connect the dots on the flow of funds.

Cross-chain moves in Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Bitcoin and other chains have occurred over the past few days for the SOL movement. In its first three and a half days, Elliptic estimates laundering was conducted on approximately 12,000 wallets on 11 blockchains, resulting in over 40,000 transactions.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B

SOL Is Being Split, Routed and Converted Into Bitcoin

Solana has become one of the active laundering routes. By November 3, about 87,000 SOL, worth roughly $8 million, had left the original theft wallet, according to Elliptic. This money was spread out for new addresses, turned into lending vaults and a liquid-staking service after which it was offered or exchanged for Bitcoin.

There was then a total of approximately 825,000 SOL in those addresses, the majority being held in two. The new entry into Privacy Cash seems to be a ploy to strengthen the embezzlement of funds while obscuring the obvious connection between incoming and outgoing transactions.

Laundering Network Already Spans Thousands of Wallets

Most beginning washing was done via Tron. The stolen TRX was spread out among roughly 7,700 TRX addresses and parts of its value were converted into Ethereum. Through various cross-chain bridges, at least $147 million has been withdrawn from Tron so far.

The aggressor has also switched both the assets and the networks by leveraging decentralized exchanges, lending platforms, and cross-chain swap services many times. The mixing of bitcoins started on the 1st of November. By early November 2, approximately 28 BTC worth of approximately $2.2 million went through a total of 18 CoinJoin transactions of WabiSabi variety.

The activity conveys the impression of being very automated, features set transaction patterns, amounts and the speed of wallet generation, Elliptic said. The quick operation resulted in approximately 32,000 transactions on Tron, the highest of which occurred at 1300 transactions per hour.

$3.18B in Stolen Crypto Still Remains Onchain

Regardless of the amount of laundering, the bulk of the stolen crypto isn’t out of the vault yet. As of Nov. 3, Elliptic estimated that $3.18 billion was left in theft-connected addresses, most of it in ETH and BTC. An additional $2.85 billion was already frozen or seized.

So far only minimal amounts have been on to a cash-out channel, the firm said. That means centralized exchanges and OTC brokers are essential places to catch and freeze.

PANAMA CITY, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its Bitbase Points program, which is designed to reward sustained participation over time. Over the 26-week season, which ends on May 4, 2027, Bitbase will distribute 1,000,000 points each week, allocated daily according to each participant’s contribution.

Four sources of contribution

Each participant’s contribution is drawn from four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Consistent activity is counted as a separate source, so continued participation from day to day adds to a user’s contribution. All eligible users, whether new to Bitbase or already active on the platform, are enrolled automatically.

For each new user referred directly, the referrer receives an additional 25% of that user’s contribution. The new user’s own points are not affected.

Participants will also receive a Trading Identity card, a shareable summary of their trading style. The first cards will be issued on November 9, with new cards following each Monday for the remainder of the season.

Existing users begin with points already credited

Before the season began, Bitbase credited points to eligible existing users based on their earlier activity on the platform. As a result, these users enter ORIGIN with their prior activity already reflected in their points and ranking.

The first program under Bitbase 2.0

On November 2, the exchange introduced Bitbase 2.0, updating its brand, app and website under the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” ORIGIN is the first program to put that statement into practice. While markets move continuously, Bitbase has chosen to assess participation across months rather than individual moments.

“We designed ORIGIN for users who participate consistently, not only during the busiest periods in the market,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “Over a six-month season, that consistency carries weight. Our responsibility is to make sure every contribution is credited, from the first day of the season to the last.”

Points and rankings are available in the Bitbase app and at bitbase.com/points.

About Bitbase

Bitbase is a digital asset exchange serving individual and institutional users worldwide, with products spanning Spot, Futures, TradFi and Earn. Bitbase aims to give users a stable and straightforward trading experience, in line with its brand statement, “Market Flows. We Focus.” Learn more at bitbase.com.

Ahead of the launch, the digital asset exchange credited points to eligible users who had been trading on the platform, so their past activity counts from day one. The season runs for 2...
content:
Panama City, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its new Bitbase Points program. Ahead of the launch, the digital asset exchange credited points to eligible users who had been trading on the platform, so their past activity counts from day one. The season runs for 26 weeks, until May 4, 2027, with 1,000,000 points distributed each week.

Part of Bitbase 2.0

ORIGIN is also the first part of Bitbase 2.0 to reach users directly. Bitbase unveiled 2.0 on November 2, with an upgraded app and website and a new brand identity built around the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” The idea is that markets will always move, and Bitbase chooses to focus on what lasts for its users. ORIGIN applies the same thinking to participation. Rather than rewarding a single burst of activity, it looks at what users do day after day over six months and credits the contribution they make across that period.

How participation is counted

Bitbase built ORIGIN around what users already do on the exchange. Eligible users, new or existing, are enrolled automatically, with no separate registration. Points are allocated daily based on each participant’s contribution, which draws on four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Because consistency is one of those sources, steady participation adds up over the course of the season.

ORIGIN also rewards users who bring others to Bitbase. A referrer receives an additional 25% of the contribution of each new user they refer directly, while the new user’s own contribution is unaffected.

Starting November 9, participants will also receive a shareable Trading Identity card that reflects their trading habits, with a new card issued every Monday until the season ends.

Recognition that continues through the season

“Bitbase 2.0 is about focus, and for our users, that means knowing their steady participation is recognized and credited,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “That’s why ORIGIN started by crediting what users had already done with us. It doesn’t ask anyone to trade differently. It simply records the participation that’s already there, every day, for the next six months.”

Users can track their points and rankings in the Bitbase app and on the website. Full details are available at bitbase.com/points.

Bitbase is a digital asset exchange serving individual and institutional users worldwide, with products spanning Spot, Futures, TradFi and Earn. title: eToro Agrees to Acquire Argentine Fintech LB Finanzas
summary:
eToro has agreed to acquire Argentine financial app LB Finanzas for an undisclosed amount, marking the trading platform’s fourth acquisition of 2026. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions.
The deal is intended to strengthen eToro’s localised presence in Latin America, with ...
content:
2026-11-04T16:03:19.756+02:00

Wednesday, 04/11/2026 | 14:03 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • The buyout will enable the trading platform to establish a localised presence in Latin America.
  • The deal follows eToro’s 2026 acquisitions of Zengo, Bit2C and an agreement to buy TradeZero

eToro has agreed to acquire Argentine financial app LB Finanzas for an undisclosed amount, marking the trading platform’s fourth acquisition of 2026. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions.

The deal is intended to strengthen eToro’s localised presence in Latin America, with eToro saying the acquisition will support its expansion in one of the region’s fast-growing fintech markets.

Accelerating Growth in Latin America

For eToro, the strategic value lies in LB Finanzas’ established local operations. Argentina’s financial environment is shaped by strict currency controls and distinctive inflation dynamics, making locally regulated infrastructure and market expertise particularly valuable.

LB Finanzas is regulated by Argentina’s National Securities Commission and Central Bank and operates an all-in-one investment platform, covering investing, such as equities and crypto, and payment solutions.

“This acquisition marks an important step in our commitment to building a localised presence in Latin America,” said Yoni Assia, eToro’s co-founder and CEO. “By combining LB Finanzas’ local expertise with eToro’s global scale, we can accelerate our growth across the region and provide more people with access to the tools they need to build their wealth.”

A Year of Acquisitions

The deal extends a busy year of inorganic growth for eToro, which has used acquisitions to add product and geographic capabilities.

In April, eToro agreed to acquire self-custodial crypto wallet provider Zengo. In May, it completed the acquisition of Israeli crypto exchange Bit2C. In August, it announced an agreement to acquire US brokerage TradeZero, a deal expected to close in the first half of 2027 and subject to regulatory approvals.

By adding local payments, crypto and wealth products to its multi-asset trading offering, eToro is broadening its platform beyond trading and investing.

The LB Finanzas deal signals a further step toward a more integrated financial-services offering in Latin America.

title: Apple Bars Staff From Using Company Secrets on Prediction Markets
summary:
Apple has told its employees they may not use confidential company information to bet on prediction markets. The rule is new in the insider trading policy that the iPhone maker filed yesterday (Tuesday) with its annual report to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
The clause brings even...
content:
2026-11-04T15:13:14.977+02:00

Wednesday, 04/11/2026 | 13:13 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The updated insider trading policy covers event contracts and applies whether or not a bet breaks securities law.
  • Emcor, GoDaddy and Seagate wrote similar rules this spring as the CFTC and Congress look into insider bets.

Apple has told its employees they may not use confidential company information to bet on prediction markets. The rule is new in the insider trading policy that the iPhone maker filed yesterday (Tuesday) with its annual report to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The clause brings event contracts into a document that had dealt only with trading in securities.

Trading on prediction markets has grown quickly. Combined taker volume at Kalshi, Polymarket and Polymarket's US venue reached $172.4 billion in the third quarter, up from $98.5 billion in the second, FM Intelligence calculations show.

Company information has already been traded on such platforms. A Polymarket user allegedly netted more than $1 million betting on Google's Year in Search rankings, a case that fed accusations of trading on nonpublic information in January.

Federal regulators treat that conduct as illegal. David Miller, enforcement director at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC ), called insider trading on Kalshi and Polymarket illegal in March and listed it first among the agency's top five enforcement priorities.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Suppliers and Carriers Fall Under the Ban

The policy covers directors, officers, employees, contractors and consultants, plus family members who live with them. The previous version of the policy, dated September 2024, did not mention prediction markets or event contracts.

Covered people may not bet on or trade event contracts using Apple Confidential Information, a category set out in the company's Business Conduct Policy that includes, but is not limited to, material nonpublic information.

The ban reaches information about other companies learned at Apple, including suppliers, manufacturers, vendors and customers such as cellular network carriers. Staff also may not pass that information to others who trade on these platforms.

The prohibition applies "whether or not the activity constitutes insider trading or securities trading under applicable laws," the policy says.

Under the general terms of the policy, Apple personnel who break it may face disciplinary action, including dismissal and repayment of equity awards.

Emcor, GoDaddy and Seagate Wrote Similar Rules

Apple is not the first US-listed company to write prediction markets into its rules this year. Bloomberg Law named several in May, and their rules differ in what information they cover.

Emcor Group amended its insider trading policy on April 2 to ban prediction market trades involving nonpublic information, according to that report. GoDaddy said in an April 24 proxy statement that its insider trading policy covers prediction markets.

Seagate Technology named Polymarket and Kalshi in a May 1 code of conduct update that bans "speculative activities where Seagate is the subject."

Seagate's quoted rule centers on bets about Seagate itself. Apple's extends to bets built on what employees learn about suppliers and carriers, and it applies whether or not a bet counts as insider trading.

Platforms Have Tightened Their Own Rules

The exchanges have moved in parallel. Polymarket's rules, updated in March, ban trading on stolen confidential information and on illegal tips, as well as trading by anyone able to influence an outcome.

Kalshi has already sanctioned a trader over bets tied to his employer. It fined a YouTube channel editor $20,397.58 and suspended him for two years for trading contracts tied to the channel where he worked, citing misuse of material nonpublic information.

Lawmakers are collecting evidence too. The House Oversight Committee asked both platforms in May for records on how they detect insider trading, with documents due by June 5.

title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Can BTC Reclaim $80K as US Midterm Election 2026 Fears Fade?
summary: Bitcoin recovered above $78,000 on November 4 after an election-night decline below $76,000, leaving traders focused on whether renewed spot demand can sustain the rebound.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin recovered above $78,000 on November 4 after an election-night decline below $76,000, leaving traders focused on whether renewed spot demand can sustain the rebound.

The US midterm election results initially triggered another wave of selling, but BTC quickly recovered as political uncertainty eased. Spot buying pressure, moving-average support, and liquidation levels are now shaping the short-term Bitcoin price prediction, with $80,000 remaining an important upside threshold.

Bitcoin Price Today Rebounds as Election Uncertainty Fades

Bitcoin experienced sharp volatility as the 2026 US midterm election results emerged. BTC traded near $78,000 before losing ground as early results indicated a Democratic victory in both chambers of Congress. The selling accelerated overnight on November 3 and pushed the Bitcoin price to approximately $75,618 on Bitstamp, its lowest level in almost seven weeks.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

However, buyers quickly entered the market near the $76,000 region. Bitcoin subsequently recovered toward $78,000, reversing much of its election-related decline. Reuters reported that BTC reached approximately $78,354 on Wednesday, November 4, while Ethereum also recovered alongside other digital assets.

The initial reaction reflected concerns about potential changes to US cryptocurrency policy under a Democratic-controlled Congress. However, market participants had already anticipated much of the election outcome, limiting the possibility of prolonged selling once the results became clearer.

Kelly Ye, head of research at Talos, highlighted this positioning in comments to Cointelegraph. She noted that Bitcoin’s post-election movement was close to what options markets had anticipated, adding that “the election was the main event, but markets had largely prepared for it.”

The recovery suggests that traders are beginning to shift their attention from election-related uncertainty toward technical levels and underlying demand. Nevertheless, reclaiming $80,000 would require additional buying pressure rather than simply reversing the latest decline.

Bitcoin Spot Buying Pressure Contrasts With Futures Selling

Trading activity across spot and derivatives markets is offering another indication of Bitcoin’s short-term direction. Crypto trader Ted Pillows shared a 15-minute BTC chart on November 4 showing positive spot cumulative volume delta (CVD) of approximately $218 million against negative futures CVD of around $482 million.

The analysis indicates limited further downside from the election outcome, with the chart showing a recovery following a sharp intraday decline. Source: Ted via X

CVD measures the difference between aggressive buying and selling activity over a selected period. Positive spot CVD indicates that market participants are placing more aggressive buy orders than sell orders in the spot market. Meanwhile, negative futures CVD reflects greater selling pressure across derivatives trading.

The divergence suggests that spot buyers are absorbing some of the selling activity generated in futures markets. This distinction is important because a recovery supported by actual spot purchases can have a different market structure from one driven primarily by leveraged positions.

Ted Pillows described the spot buying pressure as encouraging and argued that the Democratic election victory had largely been priced into the market. The accompanying chart showed Bitcoin recovering after an intraday decline, indicating that buyers were willing to enter at lower prices.

However, positive spot CVD does not guarantee a sustained reversal. The indicator reflects activity during a specific period and may change as market conditions evolve. Continued spot accumulation, accompanied by improving derivatives positioning, would provide stronger evidence that the recovery is gaining traction.

BTC Reclaims 100-Day Moving Average After Election Dip

Bitcoin’s daily chart is showing an important technical development following the election-related volatility. According to TradingShot’s TradingView analysis, BTC briefly dropped below its 100-day moving average before recovering rapidly after the election results.

BTC briefly fell below its daily MA100 but rebounded sharply, recovering all losses following the U.S. midterm election results. Source: TradingShot on TradingView 

This marked the first break below the daily 100-day moving average since August 19, when Bitcoin began a strong recovery from its previous bear-market bottom. The subsequent rebound has brought the technical indicator back into focus as traders assess whether the latest decline was a temporary breakdown or the beginning of a deeper correction.

The distinction between these scenarios will depend on Bitcoin’s ability to maintain its position above the moving average. A sustained hold could support further recovery and improve the medium-term price structure. Conversely, another decisive daily close below the indicator would weaken the bullish interpretation.

TradingShot also compared the latest price structure with a previous May decline. The analysis identified a similar 12.81% retracement toward the 100-day moving average, raising the possibility of another corrective phase if support fails.

If selling pressure returns, the 200-day moving average becomes an additional technical reference. TradingShot also highlighted the weekly 100-day moving average and the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement level as potential areas for buyers to defend.

These levels should be treated as technical reference points rather than guaranteed reversal zones. Bitcoin’s reaction around the daily 100-day moving average will provide further information about the strength of the current recovery.

Trader Realized Price Offers Another BTC Support Test

On-chain metrics are providing additional context for Bitcoin’s recent price movements. CryptoQuant highlights analyst TraderGemini’s report that BTC was trading close to its Trader On-chain Realized Price, an indicator measuring the average acquisition cost of coins that last moved between one and three months ago.

Bitcoin is testing its Trader Realized Price, which represents the average cost basis of coins last moved on-chain 1–3 months ago. Source: CryptoQuant via X

The metric provides an estimate of the cost basis for relatively recent market participants. When Bitcoin trades above this level, recent buyers generally remain in profit. This can encourage them to maintain their positions and potentially provide support during market corrections.

However, a sustained move below the Trader Realized Price could change investor behavior. Recent buyers may begin facing unrealized losses, increasing the possibility of selling pressure if the price fails to recover.

CryptoQuant’s historical chart shows that this cost-basis indicator has previously acted as support and resistance during different Bitcoin market cycles. Its current proximity to the BTC price therefore makes the level particularly relevant to the short-term outlook.

TraderGemini emphasized that holding this level and moving higher would indicate that the average cost basis of recent participants continues to support the market. A breakdown, followed by an unsuccessful recovery, could instead weaken the current bullish structure.

The indicator does not establish whether Bitcoin has reached a market bottom. Its value lies in showing how recent investors are positioned and whether their average acquisition price continues to attract buying interest.

$82K Liquidity Cluster Puts $80K Resistance in Focus

Bitcoin’s liquidation heatmap is highlighting another potential development for the coming sessions. Ted Pillows noted that BTC recently swept downside liquidity during its decline, leaving a concentrated cluster of leveraged positions around $82,000.

Bitcoin’s recent downside liquidity sweep has formed a large liquidity cluster near $82K, potentially attracting price higher and setting up a breakout attempt above $80K. Source: Ted via X

The CoinGlass heatmap covering October 21 to November 4 shows concentrations of leveraged liquidation levels across the $80,000–$85,000 region. These areas can attract the market’s attention because rapid price movements toward concentrated positions may trigger liquidations and increase trading activity.

With Bitcoin recovering from below $76,000, the $80,000 threshold represents the first important psychological and technical obstacle. A sustained move above this level could bring the higher liquidity concentration closer into focus, including the area around $82,000.

CoinDesk also highlighted the $80,000–$82,000 range as overhead resistance in its November 4 market analysis. Markus Thielen, founder of 10x Research, pointed to Bitcoin’s daily stochastic indicator, which suggested that the cryptocurrency had become oversold during the decline.

Thielen identified $82,000 as a potential recovery target based on the momentum reading. However, this remains an analyst’s technical assessment rather than confirmation that Bitcoin will reach that level.

Liquidation heatmaps also require careful interpretation. They estimate where leveraged positions may be concentrated, but these clusters can shift as traders open, close, or adjust their positions. They should not be treated as fixed price targets.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: Can BTC Reclaim $80K?

Bitcoin’s immediate outlook depends on whether buyers can maintain the recovery and overcome resistance around $80,000. The latest spot CVD reading, the rebound above the daily 100-day moving average, and the recovery from the election-night low provide several encouraging technical signals.

A sustained move above $78,000 would help strengthen the short-term recovery structure. If buying pressure continues, BTC could challenge $80,000 before testing the $81,900–$82,000 region. The latter area also aligns with the 50-day moving average near $81,911 in a contemporaneous November 4 technical assessment.

Nevertheless, the broader market structure remains vulnerable. Bitcoin’s recent decline showed that election-related headlines can quickly influence leveraged trading, while the presence of overhead selling pressure could restrict further gains.

On the downside, the $76,000 region remains an important area to monitor. Bitcoin’s election-night low near $75,618 and the 50-week moving average around $75,733 provide additional support references. A decisive breakdown below these levels could expose the longer-term 200-day moving average near $73,163.

Spot demand will also remain important. While Ted Pillows’ chart indicates that buyers have been active in the spot market, sustained recovery would benefit from continued accumulation and improving institutional investment flows.

CoinDesk reported that US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced approximately $515 million in outflows during October, followed by substantial withdrawals during the first two trading days of November. These figures suggest that institutional demand remains an important factor to watch as BTC attempts to regain higher price levels.

For now, Bitcoin’s recovery has reduced immediate election-related selling pressure, but it has not established a confirmed medium-term bullish reversal. Reclaiming $80,000 and maintaining support around the moving averages would provide stronger evidence of improving market conditions. Until then, the $76,000–$82,000 range remains an important area for monitoring the next phase of Bitcoin price action.

title: The Trading Festival Mexico's Trading Cup Offers Traders a Shot at a 100K Challenge
summary: The Trading Cup will bring live trading competition to The Trading Festival Mexico 2026, powered by iFX EXPO, on 12–13 November at the World Trade Center Mexico City. Sponsored by The5ers, the two-day tournament will give eligible participants the opportunity to test their strategies in a demo tradi...
