title: Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation
summary:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell
The post Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation appeared first on Cry...
content:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell players to trust that every result is random. Now, with these systems, there’s a way for them to verify outcomes independently. By applying this technology to their original games, it combines familiar gaming formats with a more transparent approach to game results.

The following crypto platforms are leading the way in showcasing the industry’s latest innovation.

  • Duel
  • Thrill
  • Winna
  • Yeet

Duel

At the forefront of this movement is Duel. Play Duel’s provably fair online games, and you’ll see it is possible to verify the outcomes of its games. That means you can see everything was generated fairly and not simply accept the platform’s word. Before a round, Duel generates a server seed. This is joined by a player-provided client seed and nonce, which increases with each round. It also publishes a SHA-256 hash of the server seed before play, creating a commitment that can be checked later.

After the game, Duel reveals the unhashed server seed. You can compare it with the original hash and verify that the combined seeds and nonce produce the recorded result. This hands you a practical way to check the outcome generation process, with a built-in verifier making the process more accessible. The system applies to each of the 12 “Duel Originals”. Those games also stand out for their 100% RTP, which removes the platform’s mathematical advantage. A one-of-a-kind aspect you won’t find elsewhere, it shows Duel goes to the next level for fair gameplay.

Thrill

Thrill also applies provably fair mechanics to its own in-house games. From Dice to Crash, these titles stick with clear outcomes and straightforward rules. That makes them a natural fit for systems that allow players to check how results are generated. Provably fair technology, naturally, adds a verification layer to the gaming experience. Then with Thrill’s XP progression system and weekly races, there are other reasons for players to return.

Winna

Provably fair is also part of the original games found at Winna. From revealing tiles in Mines to watching a ball bounce through Plinko’s pegs, these in-house titles keep it simple with a decision- or chance-based outcome. The value of provably fair technology here is that players have a way to check results on their own. Like Duel, Winna combines these games with a wider crypto gaming platform and sports-related features for multiple interactive options.

Yeet

Combining sports-related features and crypto gaming with its own originals, Yeet includes in-house creations like Dice and Plinko. As these simple formats place the outcome at the center of the experience, transparency is a key aspect. With its provably fair technology implementation, players gain a method for checking game results. Its originals provide an alternative to its wider selection of third-party titles, while the sports-related section expands the platform beyond its original games.

Provably fair technology gives players a way to verify game outcomes. However, it’s important to highlight that it doesn’t guarantee winning. Even if you check ten wins or ten losses in a row, it plays no part in the next result.

title: What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked
summary:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call
The post What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call the bank and move on. With a crypto card, the stakes can feel higher, because crypto payments are hard or impossible to reverse.

The good news is that most crypto card problems are fixable if you act quickly and in the right order. The key is understanding what was actually exposed, because a lost card and a hacked wallet are very different problems. Here is exactly what to do in each case.

  • First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk
  • If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen
  • If Someone Is Using Your Card Online
  • If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked
  • Beware of Recovery Scams
  • How to Prevent It Happening Again
  • Frequently Asked Questions

First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk

Before you panic, separate the card from the crypto behind it.

SituationWhat is exposedUrgency
Physical card lostThe card number and limitsHigh, but contained
Card details stolen onlineCard paymentsHigh, but contained
App or account login compromisedYour card balance and settingsVery high
Wallet seed phrase exposedEvery coin in that walletCritical

A lost plastic card is usually the least dangerous of these. Someone holding it can try to make card payments, but they cannot empty your wallet with it. A leaked seed phrase is the opposite. Whoever has it controls your funds, and no card freeze will stop them.

If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen

Speed matters most in the first few minutes.

  1. Freeze the card in the app. Nearly every crypto card app has an instant freeze toggle. Use it before anything else, since you can unfreeze it if the card turns up.
  2. Check recent transactions. Look for anything you did not make, and screenshot it.
  3. Contact support. Report the card lost or stolen through the app or the issuer’s official support channel, never a number from a search ad.
  4. Order a replacement. A new card comes with a new number, and the old one is cancelled.
  5. Use the virtual card meanwhile. Many providers issue a virtual card you can add to Apple Pay or Google Pay right away.

Cards that spend directly from your own wallet carry an extra advantage here. With a self-custody Crypto Debit Card, your coins stay in the wallet you control rather than in a separate card account, so a lost card does not hand anyone your funds. Freezing the card cuts off spending, and the crypto never moved. 

If Someone Is Using Your Card Online

Unauthorized charges mean your card details have leaked, often through a breached shop, a phishing page, or malware.

    • Freeze the card and request a new number
    • Report each unauthorized payment to the issuer and ask about dispute options
  • Change the password on your card app and turn on two-factor authentication
  • Scan your devices for malware, and remove browser extensions you do not recognize

Card-network payments sometimes have dispute processes, but support varies widely between crypto card providers. Report quickly, because most dispute windows are short.

If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked

This is the serious scenario, and it needs a different response.

If your card app login was compromised, change the password immediately, revoke all active sessions, and reset two-factor authentication from a device you trust. Then contact support to lock the account while you investigate.

If your wallet seed phrase or private key was exposed, act as if the wallet is already lost. Create a brand-new wallet with a new seed phrase on a clean device, and move any remaining funds into it right away. Then reconnect your card to the new wallet. Do not try to “secure” the old wallet. Once a seed phrase leaks, that wallet can never be trusted again.

Beware of Recovery Scams

Right after a theft is when the second scam usually arrives. People who post about lost crypto online are quickly targeted by “recovery experts” promising to trace and return stolen funds for an upfront fee. They cannot. The FTC’s guide on what to know about cryptocurrency and scams notes that crypto payments typically cannot be reversed, and that anyone guaranteeing to recover your money is a red flag.

Report real theft to your card provider, the police, and the FTC or your country’s equivalent. Never pay someone who contacts you offering to get your crypto back.

How to Prevent It Happening Again

A few habits make a big difference:

  • Turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, not SMS
  • Never store your seed phrase in photos, notes apps, or cloud storage
  • Set spending limits and transaction alerts in your card app
  • Use the virtual card for online shopping and keep the physical card for in-person payments
  • Keep most of your crypto in a separate wallet from your spending balance

If you are still deciding which card to use, it helps to start by comparing the top crypto cards on security features as well as fees and rewards. Instant freeze controls, real-time alerts, and self-custody spending are worth as much as a higher cashback rate on the day something goes wrong.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can someone steal my crypto with just my card?

Usually not. A physical card or its number can be used for card payments within its limits, but it does not give access to your wallet. Your seed phrase and app login are the real keys to your funds.

Can I get my money back after an unauthorized crypto card payment?

Sometimes. Card-network payments may be eligible for a dispute, depending on your provider’s policy. Report the charge immediately, since dispute windows are often short.

Should I freeze or cancel my card?

Freeze it first. Freezing is instant and reversible if the card turns up. Cancel and replace it once you confirm it is truly lost or that the details were stolen, and update any subscriptions linked to the old number.

Is it safe to use a recovery service for stolen crypto?

No. Services that promise to recover stolen crypto for an upfront fee are almost always scams. Report the theft to your provider and the authorities instead.

title: Pghinvestment and the Retail Investors the Market Was Not Built For
summary: The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a brok...
content:
Skip to content

The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a broker or an adviser. What they frequently do not arrive with is formal financial education.

That is not a criticism of them. It is a description of a market that opened up faster than the teaching around it did, and it leaves platforms holding a question they did not previously have to answer: what do you owe someone who is capable, motivated and underprepared all at once.

Most of the industry has answered that question with content. Webinars, glossaries, a learning tab nobody opens twice.

The more telling answer is structural. It shows up in how an account behaves, not in what the marketing says about education.

What the participation data actually shows

The World Economic Forum, in its Global Retail Investor Outlook, describes a new wave of participants drawn from groups the industry historically underserved, including younger investors and people in emerging markets, and names limited financial education and the complexity of evolving technology among the obstacles they meet. The audience is widening in exactly the places where support has always been thinnest.

The World Federation of Exchanges reaches a complementary conclusion from the market side. Reviewing retail trading across its member exchanges, it finds that retail participation improves liquidity and the depth of the order book, while stating directly that it may increase volatility and must be complemented with strong investor protection policies. More participation is only a good outcome when something is built to carry it.

Learning without paying for the lesson

This is where Pghinvestment has made a choice that reads as a product decision but functions as an educational one. Its practice environment runs on the conditions a funded account actually sees, so the pricing and execution a client meets while testing are the ones waiting for them afterwards.

That distinction matters more than it sounds. A rehearsal that flatters the trader is not neutral. It is misleading, because it produces a confidence the market never agreed to.

Experts at Pghinvestment treat that fidelity as the whole point of the feature, not a technical detail buried inside it, which is why the practice environment sits alongside the live Pghinvestment platform rather than behind a beginner label.

The Pghinvestment entry point works in the same direction. An account can be opened without committing an amount a client would genuinely miss, which turns the first months into something a person can afford to be bad at. That is a more realistic model of how trading is actually learned than any curriculum.

Participation before mastery

There is a second route through the preparedness gap, and it is the one Pghinvestment leans on hardest: it does not insist on mastery as the price of entry.

Its managed structures let someone take part while they are still learning, instead of making them wait until they are not. PAMM and MAM arrangements place capital alongside a more experienced trader while the owner keeps sight of what is happening to it, and Copy Trading mirrors selected positions as they occur.

Used well, the Pghinvestment managed structures amount to a form of apprenticeship. A client watching decisions get made on their own balance, in markets they are still reading, learns something a tutorial cannot teach. The framing from Pghinvestment is consistent with that: these structures are presented as a route into participation while understanding builds, not as a reason to stop building it.

One environment, widening scope

There is a quieter benefit in the breadth of the Pghinvestment account range. Currencies, equities, metals, indices, commodities and digital assets sit behind one login, which means a client broadening their exposure is not also learning an unfamiliar system at the same moment they are learning an unfamiliar market.

The thing that changes is the instrument, not the interface. For someone who arrived through digital assets and is now looking at metals or indices for the first time, removing that second layer of unfamiliarity is worth more than it appears on a feature comparison.

Funding runs through card, bank transfer or digital currency, with nothing added by Pghinvestment to make a deposit. Withdrawal thresholds are set low, which keeps the arrangement workable for clients operating at modest size while they find their footing.

Where this leaves the industry

Instrument counts will keep getting longer across the industry, and they will keep mattering less than how a platform behaves in a client’s first six months. The firms that come out of this period with retained clients will be the ones that planned for people learning the job while doing it. Judged on how Pghinvestment has assembled its practice conditions, its managed routes in and its entry pricing, that looks like the assumption it started from.

title: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance was able to resume withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks. More than $5.8 billion in net withdrawals were seen over the 24 hours, as tracked by DefiLlama. The
The post Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance was able to resume withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks.
  • More than $5.8 billion in net withdrawals were seen over the 24 hours, as tracked by DefiLlama.
  • The exchange is recovering from the record $6.3 billion crypto theft.

Binance is gradually resuming crypto withdrawals following one of the largest security breaches in the crypto industry’s history, the latest among which are Zcash, TON, and Sui. Meanwhile, billions of dollars are flowing out of the exchange and Binance’s liquidity and user confidence are subject to close scrutiny.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Reopens Withdrawals Across 15 Crypto Networks
  • Stablecoins Return Across Major Chains
    • Binance Sees Billions Leave After $6.3B Hack
    • Withdrawal Recovery Becomes a Test of Binance Liquidity

Binance Reopens Withdrawals Across 15 Crypto Networks

Binance’s latest update added withdrawals for ZEC on Zcash, USDT and GRAM on TON, and SUI on Sui. Those are the networks that are linked to Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, XRP Ledger, Base, Dogecoin, Optimism, Arbitrum, Tron, Solana, Polygon and Avalanche C-Chain.

Latest Withdrawal Update

Withdrawals have now been re-enabled for the following networks and assets:

New:
✅ ZEC: ZEC
✅ TON: USDT, GRAM
✅ SUI: SUI

Already Enabled:
✅ BTC: BTC
✅ ETH: ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ BSC: BNB, USDT, USDC
✅ XRP: XRP
✅ Base: ETH, USDC
✅ DOGE: DOGE
✅ OP (Optimism): ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ ARBITRUM: ARB, ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ TRX: TRX, USDT
✅ SOL: SOL, USDT, USDC
✅ MATIC (Polygon): POL, USDT, USDC
✅ AVAXC: AVAX, USDT, USDC

We will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases as security checks are completed. Further updates will be shared through official Binance channels.

— Binance (@binance) November 1, 2026

According to the exchange, it is attempting to restore the networks on a phased basis and every network is going through security and stability tests before withdrawals are turned on.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Stablecoins Return Across Major Chains

Withdrawals of USDT and USDC are already enabled on several of Binance’s biggest supported networks, such as Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Polygon and Arbitrum.

This is particularly significant since they are a significant proportion of exchange liquidity and are frequently utilized by traders swapping assets between exchange spots. Binance has announced that more assets and networks will be returning once more checks are made.

Binance Sees Billions Leave After $6.3B Hack

Heavy withdrawal activity that orchestrated the reopening. DEFLI has recorded $5.8 billion in net outflows, while Binance has recorded roughly $3.64 billion in net outflows. Binance has an estimated $171 billion worth of customer assets, and the official net outflow was around 2.1% of the total customer assets, according to Reuters.

Withdrawals came after a massive security breach where approximately $6.3 billion in crypto assets were stolen.

The FBI blamed TraderTraitor hackers, linked to a North Korean insurgency, for the attack, said Reuters. Binance, in turn, has responded that it covered approximately $6 billion of the lost assets with its Secure Asset Fund for Users and futures insurance fund.

Withdrawal Recovery Becomes a Test of Binance Liquidity

One of the most definitive signs of user responses to the hack is the rate of withdrawals. People have requested withdrawals in large numbers after Binance resumed operations, but the withdrawals seem to have settled down in recent times, Binance stated. Meanwhile, gross withdrawals did not affect overall exchange reserves, as deposits kept coming in.

In the wake of the exchange, new hot wallet addresses have also had to be created as a security response and uploaded into the exchanges Proof of Reserves infrastructure.

The big one for traders will be what happens to the flow of funds as the rest of the networks are all back. In the meantime, Binance’s gradual reopening is a serious exercise in how effective its reserves, security measures, and customer faith will be if a massive attack is implemented.

title: Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance
summary:
Key Takeaways: On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks. Eighteen years later, Bitcoin
The post Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance appe...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks.
  • Eighteen years later, Bitcoin developed from a novel monetary system to an asset owned by public organizations, investment funds, and governments.
  • Bitcoin Archive celebrated the occasion on its X page, restating the bold conclusion that the crypto industry began.

Bitcoin’s whitepaper was created on October 31st, 2008, marking 18 years in digital asset history. The initial allotment of nine pages of documents to send the funds without any process of money brokering has now become a worldwide network of trillions of dollars’ worth.

  • Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money
  • Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community
    • The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money

On October 31, 2008, an individual or group using the name Satoshi Nakamoto published Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System on a cryptography mailing list.

One major problem with online payments was that too often, financial institutions had to confirm the transfers of funds and avoid double spending. Satoshi envisioned a new peer-to-peer system that did not require central control to function: When people make an exchange, the transaction is verified using cryptographic proof, with a shared and publicly visible record containing the transactions.

This design was a distributed ledger plus proof-of-work. The miners confirm transactions, create new blocks, and miners are rewarded with transactions whenever the network follows the longest chain with largest proof-of-work.

On January 3, 2009, the Bitcoin network came into operation by mining the first block. This protocol later comes to be associated with a maximum supply of 21 million BTC and the assets are issued at a predictable time frame.

Read More: Michael Saylor Teases More Bitcoin After Strategy’s $69.45B Reserve Hits 848,250 BTC

Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community

The network has since expanded well beyond the realm of cryptography, where the paper first appeared. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024, providing another channel for traditional investors to buy Bitcoin without owning cryptocurrency wallets.

Public companies are also including Bitcoin on their balance sheets. Some other examples include strategy being the largest publicly listed corporate holder and the U.S. government creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve in March 2025 using seized Bitcoins.

This represents a significant shift from Bitcoin’s early years, when every Bitcoin was dominated by technology enthusiasts and early adopters.

The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Bitcoin Archive recently marked the occasion on X with a message celebrating 18 years of Bitcoin and thanking Satoshi Nakamoto. Another aspect of the network’s creation was also touched on in the post, the historic moment.

18 years of Bitcoin.

Thank you, Satoshi — what an incredible journey. https://t.co/DhYNB3SZ9y

— Bitcoin Archive (@BitcoinArchive) October 31, 2026

However, Bitcoin’s original concept has stayed true to its nature, allowing users to make transactions on a public network without a bank or payment company approving it.

Satoshi’s identity remains unknown, and the white paper’s publication began a project that would eventually influence thousands of other digital assets and blockchain networks.

title: Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing
summary:
Key Takeaways: The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing. All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk. The
The post Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing.
  • All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk.
  • The consultation will be open until Feb. 12, 2027.

The Bank of England comes closer and closer to introducing tokenized assets into the mainstream of the UK market infrastructure.

The central bank has launched a consultation outlining how central counterparties, or CCPs, could accept tokenized versions of eligible collateral without creating a separate regulatory regime for blockchain-based assets.

  • Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral
  • Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome
    • Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later
    • UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral

The proposal concentrates on assets that are or could be already collaterized according to the UK’s CCP.

The Bank says tokenization by itself won’t bar an asset from being accepted. What’s important is whether the collateral remains easily transferable and saleable, has little credit risk and market risk, and can still be valued.

The Bank has reported that tokenization of collateral can facilitate trades of assets across markets and jurisdictions, particularly in meeting margin calls. Faster collateral movement could also reduce operational friction in clearing and support wider adoption of digital market infrastructure.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome

The Bank is sticking to a simple rule: tokenized collateral should achieve the same regulatory result as traditional collateral. That means CCPs would need to show that digital representations of assets remain accessible and transferable even during stressed market conditions.

The regulator additionally urges firms to look at the risk associated with technology, custody arrangements and reliance on third-party infrastructure. For instance, tokenized security relying on a bridge that links blockchain records to other asset locations would require knowledge of the consequences of the bridge being compromised.

Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later

The consultation doesn’t instantly add to the list of collaterals that are eligible. It primarily concentrates on the tokenisation of assets currently allowed under the existing regulations, such as cash, financial instruments, bank guarantees and gold, provided they meet established criteria.

But also the Bank´s position is seeking input from industry on a wider array of assets that may qualify in the future. That conversation also covers tokenized money market fund shares, tokenized gold, and stablecoins, so it’s applicable to the entire crypto ecosystem.

Some digital assets could eventually comply with existing collateral standards, the Bank said, and advised firms contemplating digital assets to reach out to supervisors early on.

UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

The consultation is part of a wider consultation by the Bank of England, Financial Conduct Authority and HM Treasury in the UK. Their mission is to establish a more straightforward rule for tokenized securities and settlement in the digital medium, while fostering financial stability.

It will help foster responsible tokenization while maintaining the resilience of financial market infrastructure, said Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, Sarah Breeden. The consultation will continue through Feb. 12, 2027, and the Bank takes into account industry comments to decide its supervisory strategy.

Jupiter Lend Faces Liquidity Crunch

On October 30, Jupiter addressed withdrawal delays through its official X account, explaining that broader market conditions had created a liquidity shortage across its lending pools.

Due to broader market conditions, there is currently a liquidity crunch impacting withdrawals.

Market conditions will cause users to deposit or repay their loans. As they do so, withdrawals will be able to process again.

This is normal and expected during events like today’s. Liquidity will soon be available again.

The protocol is functioning as expected and all funds are safe.

— Jupiter Earn (@jupiter_earn) October 30, 2026

Withdrawals would be resumed as market players deposit their assets or repay their loans, the protocol said. It said the situation was normal at all times of significant market volatility and all funds belonging to users are safe.

The announcement came amid increasing security fears surrounding Binance and market actions by the broader crypto sector. Jupiter had earlier said that it was keeping an eye on development and had never had any direct exposure to Binance.

Users asked how there could be any contradiction between the earlier reassurance and the delays in withdrawal, to which Jupiter responded that both the things were correct.

It noted that Binance couldn’t raise any money and the protocol didn’t lose any. The withdrawal pressure is not directly related to the exchange incident, the team said and instead is an indicator of reactions from the wider market.

Why Are Withdrawals Being Delayed?

Jupiter Lend gifts work by means of lending pools where a deposited good can be borrowed by items like Borrow and Multiply. This is because not all deposits will be available immediately as some assets may be used to make loans on the go.

Liquidity may not keep up with the demand for it in periods of heavy withdrawal demand. The repayment of borrowers and fresh money for deposits are therefore significant in restoring withdrawal capacity.

USDC Withdrawable Balance Raises Concerns

Jupiter’s API data aptly pointed to the magnitude of the liquidity situation. Around 418.5 million USDCs in Earn deposit claims, with accrued interest, were visible at 7.14 a.m. ET, whereas 3.35 USDCs were immediately available to withdraw.

This difference reflects the amount of the claims of depositors serviceable by the bank at a given time versus the liquid funds held by the bank. That is not, however, a finding of loan impairment nor a determination that depositors have been losing money on the underlying loans.

In addition to the above, Jupiter documents further withdrawals based on available amounts and permission to withdraw. Users might have to make smaller withdrawals or wait for returns of liquidity.

The withdrawal scenario comes amidst worries over Binance’s security breach, estimated to cause around $6.3 billion damage to Binance.
